title: Protocol for reversible induction of hyposmia in rats using intranasal gadolinium chloride administration.
abstract: Here, we present a protocol for intranasal administration of gadolinium chloride in adult rats to induce transient olfactory dysfunction. We describe steps for preparing gadolinium chloride solution, bilateral intranasal infusion under isoflurane anesthesia, and post-infusion stabilization. We then detail procedures for animal monitoring and behavioral assessment using the hidden cookie test. The procedure produces reproducible impairment in olfactory-guided food-seeking behavior, detectable the day after administration and lasting 7 days. Behavioral performance then returns to baseline, indicating recovery of olfactory-guided function.

title: Longitudinal associations between positive life events and depression: The roles of optimism and self-schemata.
journal: Journal of psychopathology and clinical science
abstract: Relative to stress exposure and stress generation, the role of positive life events (PLEs) exposure and generation in depression is less clear. In addressing this issue, the current study examined major depression, dispositional optimism, and positive self-schemata as mechanisms of PLE generation in a sample of young adults (N = 119, 79.83% female). At baseline, participants (49.74% with current major depression) completed measures of depression, optimism, and self-schema. At 6-month follow-up, participants were administered a measure of depressive symptom severity and a contextual life event interview assessing PLEs since baseline. Dependent PLEs, specifically interpersonal dependent PLEs, prospectively predicted fewer depressive symptoms. Optimism and positive self-schemata prospectively predicted dependent PLEs, specifically interpersonal dependent PLEs. PLE generation mediated the negative association between optimism and prospective depressive symptoms. Independent PLEs were largely unassociated with PLE exposure and generation. Findings highlight the interpersonal nature of PLEs in depression. Clinical implications are discussed. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

title: Female reoffending trajectories in England from 2000 to 2021: A longitudinal administrative data study.
abstract: As women are a minority group in the criminal justice system, they have often been neglected in criminological research. Research exploring offending trajectories has largely focused on male and mixed-gender samples, and studies using female-only cohorts have been constrained by small sample sizes, short follow-ups, and limited evidence from England. This study therefore aimed to use a nationally representative sample to identify trajectories of female offending from childhood into adulthood. We expected that life-course-persistent, adolescent-limited, and adult-onset groups would be identified. This study used a linkage of the Police National Computer and the National Pupil Database to create a birth cohort of females who had offended in England (N = 196,089). The study explored their offending trajectories from the age of criminal responsibility (10 years) up to age 31 years using a latent class analysis approach. Binary indicator variables used were age of first offense (as "child: 10-13 years," "adolescent: 14-17 years," "young adult: 18-20 years," and "adult: ≥21 years"), age of last offense (as "juvenile: 10-17 years," "young adult: 18-20 years," and "adult: ≥21 years"), and being a persistent offender as "juvenile," "young adult," or "adult" (committing more than the median number of offenses). Analyses controlled for having ever been incarcerated. A four-class model was identified with the following classes: "life course persistent" (11%), "adolescent limited" (54%), "young adult limited" (16%), and "adult onset" (19%). These classes resemble those identified using male and mixed-gender samples. As rates of female imprisonment increase, it is ever more important that we attempt to understand women's engagement with the criminal justice system. By identifying the key developmental patterns of female offending in England, this study provides an empirical basis for early identification and tailored support for those women most at risk of persistent offending. title: Beyond immune suppression: Revisiting adenosine A2A receptor biology in CD8+ T-cell differentiation, metabolic fitness and cancer immunotherapy.
abstract: Extracellular adenosine is a major immunosuppressive metabolite of the tumor microenvironment and a key barrier to anti-tumor immunity. Generated from ATP by the ectonucleotidases CD39 and CD73, it signals mainly through the high-affinity A2A adenosine receptor (A2AR). Although A2AR is regarded as an inhibitory immune checkpoint, recent work shows that its functions extend beyond immediate effector suppression to the regulation of metabolic fitness, mitochondrial homeostasis, and CD8+ T-cell differentiation. Notably, both sustained A2AR activation and complete receptor deficiency can drive terminal exhaustion through distinct mechanisms, and CD73 and extracellular adenosine are not biologically equivalent. Here we summarize adenosine signaling, the cell-specific roles of the A2AR axis, and the clinical development of A2AR-targeting immunotherapies. We identify the principal obstacles to therapeutic translation and advance biomarker-guided, calibrated modulation of A2AR signaling as a testable hypothesis rather than an established therapeutic principle, one that now requires comparative exposure-response and longitudinal intervention studies.

title: Current perspectives in the pharmacological treatment of gambling disorder: psychedelics and beyond.
abstract: Gambling disorder (GD) is a heterogeneous behavioral addiction associated with dysregulated reward processing, impaired executive control, stress-system dysfunction, and maladaptive neuroplasticity. Despite its considerable clinical, social, and economic burden, no medication is currently approved specifically for GD, and available pharmacological strategies remain off label. This narrative review examines established and emerging pharmacological approaches to GD. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language literature published between January 2010 and January 2026. Opioid antagonists show the most consistent, although still limited, therapeutic signal with potential benefits in selected patients with prominent gambling urges, whereas evidence for antidepressants, mood stabilizers, antiepileptic drugs, and antipsychotics remains heterogeneous. Glutamatergic, noradrenergic, endocannabinoid, and orexin-related interventions are biologically plausible but largely experimental. Psychedelic and neuroplasticity-oriented treatments, including psilocybin, ketamine/esketamine, and 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA)-assisted interventions, may target cognitive inflexibility, compulsive behavior, and maladaptive reward learning. The available evidence supports a cautious, mechanism-informed approach to pharmacological research, while underscoring the need for adequately powered clinical trials and prospective evaluation of clinically relevant treatment-response indicators. Pharmacotherapy for GD should move toward phenotype-informed, multimodal treatment rather than a one-size-fits-all model. Emerging neuroplasticity-based interventions are promising, but adequately powered, controlled, and longitudinal trials are required before clinical implementation.

title: Azetukalner in Adults With Focal Seizures: The X-TOLE2 Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: Despite more than 30 approved antiseizure medications, many individuals with focal epilepsy continue to experience seizures, indicating a persistent need for novel therapies. To determine efficacy and safety of the novel, potent KV7 channel opener azetukalner for treatment of focal seizures. This phase 3, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial of azetukalner was conducted over a 12-week double-blind period (November 18, 2022, to February 3, 2026) at 138 sites in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia Pacific. Adults with focal epilepsy experiencing 4 or more focal seizures per month despite stable treatment with 1 to 3 antiseizure medications were enrolled. Data were analyzed using a dataset derived from the database lock dated February 26, 2026. Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to receive placebo or 15 or 25 mg of azetukalner once daily with the evening meal for 12 weeks with no titration period. Participants completing the double-blind period could enter an open-label extension. The primary efficacy end point was median percentage change from baseline in monthly (28-day) focal seizure frequency during the double-blind period for azetukalner vs placebo. Safety and tolerability were assessed by recording treatment-emergent adverse events, changes in clinical laboratory findings, vital signs, and electrocardiogram. Of 607 adults screened, 374 participants (190 [50.8%] female; mean [SD] age, 40.0 [12.9] years) were enrolled, randomized and treated with placebo (125 participants), 15-mg azetukalner (125 participants), or 25-mg azetukalner (124 participants). Participants had a baseline median (IQR) of 12.75 (7.56 to 32.97) seizures per month and had previously tried and stopped a median (IQR) of 5 (3 to 8) antiseizure medications. Most (336 participants [89.8%]) were receiving 2 to 3 concomitant antiseizure medications. The median (IQR) change from baseline in monthly seizure frequency was -10.4% (-39.1% to 8.3%) for the placebo group, -34.5% (-61.6% to -12.3%) for the 15-mg azetukalner group (P < .001 vs placebo), and -53.2% (-77.2% to -28.8%) for the 25-mg azetukalner group (P < .001 vs placebo). Azetukalner was generally well tolerated, and treatment-emergent adverse events were comparable to those observed in the phase 2b X-TOLE trial. This randomized clinical trial found that azetukalner demonstrated robust, rapid, and durable reductions in seizure frequency with a favorable benefit-risk profile. Treatment with azetukalner resulted in one of the largest median percentage reductions in seizure frequency vs placebo reported to date in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, supporting azetukalner as a promising novel antiseizure medication with significant opportunity to improve clinical outcomes. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05614063.

title: Arrival of CAR T-Cell Therapies for Stiff Person Syndrome.
Review of Gastroparesis-Reply.
Identification of RIMKLA-IgG Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndrome With Cerebellar Ataxia.
abstract: Autoimmune cerebellar ataxias are debilitating neurological syndromes that need early detection and intervention. Antineural antibodies are a crucial diagnostic marker, however, lack of knowledge of specific autoantibodies in seronegative patients remains a significant challenge. To pair a cutting-edge, standardized, and rigorous autoantibody detection pathway with global clinical networks to identify novel autoantibody markers of autoimmune ataxia. This was a multicenter case series study that included samples of patients with uncharacterized central nervous system disorders, collected between 2015 and 2020 at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF). A comprehensive screening for additional patients was conducted using a blinded cell-based and tissue-based assay in the French reference center on paraneoplastic neurological syndrome (PNS) and autoimmune encephalitis (AE). Analysis was completed in 2026. Referred participants included those with idiopathic neurological disease with suspicion of autoimmune etiology, controls with noninflammatory disease, and patients with known paraneoplastic autoantibody associations who served as positive controls. Sera and cerebrospinal fluid were collected for autoantibody screening and validation experiments. Autoantibody screening and candidate antibody validations. Detection of autoantibodies and characterization of their usefulness as biomarkers of autoimmune clinical symptoms. A total of 35 patients were referred, and 8 patients (median [IQR] age, 65 [47-74] years; 6 male [75%]) were identified to have IgG targeting the intracellular neural protein ribosomal modification protein RimK-like family member A (RIMKLA). Initially, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from a UCSF index patient with small cell lung cancer and inflammatory cerebellar ataxia showed a specific staining pattern in the deep nuclei of the cerebellum and brainstem but was seronegative on all known panels of PNS biomarkers. Subsequent screening identified 7 additional patients sharing a similar clinical profile characterized by progressive cerebellar ataxia, diplopia, cranial VI paresis, and sensory and motor abnormalities. The majority of patients (6 of 8 [75%]) had associated small cell lung cancer. All patients also exhibited inflammatory CSF and immunoglobulin synthesis. In this case series, novel PNS autoantibodies targeting the neural protein RIMKLA were identified in patients with small cell lung cancer and cerebellar ataxia. RIMKLA-IgG represents a new diagnostic biomarker for an intracellular-antigen PNS associated with cerebellar and hindbrain encephalitis with possible peripheral and motor involvement.

title: The role of central monoamines in the positive reinforcing effects of affective touch.
abstract: Affective touch can produce positive emotional states and serves as a critical component of social bonding. Although the circuitry of affective touch has been well characterized, the role of central monoamines in the functional consequences of affective touch has not been systematically examined. The objective of this study was to examine the role of monoamines in the positive reinforcing effects of affective touch METHODS: Male and female rats were treated with selective monoamine reuptake inhibitors (GBR 12909, atomoxetine, fluoxetine) and nonselective monoamine releasers/reuptake inhibitors (amphetamine, cocaine, MDMA) and placed into an apparatus divided into two equally sized areas. When rats were in the "touch" area, they were "petted" by a blinded experimenter; when rats were in the "no touch" area, they were left undisturbed. All drugs were tested across a 10-fold dose range, and saline and oxytocin were tested as negative and positive controls, respectively. Affective touch served as a positive reinforcer as indicated by a preference for the "touch" area. Oxytocin, the nonselective monoamine reuptake inhibitor cocaine, and the nonselective monoamine releaser amphetamine robustly increased the reinforcing effects of touch. To a lesser degree, the selective dopamine reuptake inhibitor GBR 12909 increased the reinforcing effects of touch, whereas the nonselective monoamine releaser/reuptake inhibitor MDMA decreased the reinforcing effects of touch. These data suggest that drugs that increase synaptic dopamine, particularly those with high addiction liability, increase the positive reinforcing effects of affective touch. These data also suggest that MDMA may not reproduce in rodents the entactogenic effects commonly reported in humans and some nonhuman primate studies.

title: Behavioural parent training for disruptive behaviour in children with autism: moderators and mediators of the effects of a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Behavioural parent training is a well-established intervention for children with autism and disruptive behaviour. In a recent randomized controlled trial on parent training for children with autism and disruptive behaviour, we found positive effects of face-to-face (but not blended) parent training on children's noncompliance and irritability, and on parenting sense of competence and overreactive parenting. However, effect sizes were medium, which may indicate room for improvement. Here, we investigated two potential avenues to achieve such improvement: (1) by getting a better understanding of the mechanisms of change of the intervention (i.e., mediation effects); (2) by identifying whether there are subgroups for whom the intervention works better or worse (i.e., moderation effects). We tested whether parenting sense of competence, parenting stress and parenting style mediated the effects of parent training on our primary outcome measures child noncompliance and irritability. In addition, we examined if parenting sense of competence, parenting stress, parenting style, parental attitudes or parental psychopathology moderated treatment success. We found that an improvement in parenting sense of competence was associated with the effect of face-to-face parent training on children's noncompliance, but not on irritability, while changes in parenting stress or parenting style were not related to treatment effects. We did not find any moderating effects on the effects of parent training. We conclude that, based on these results, more focus on increasing parents' feelings of competence as a parent might be a way forward to increase the effectiveness of behavioural parent training for children with autism and disruptive behaviour.

title: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery versus intraoperative cesium-131 brachytherapy for resected brain metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Pre-operative stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and intraoperative cesium-131 (Cs-131) brachytherapy are alternatives to post-operative SRS for resected brain metastases (BMs). The randomized phase 3 Radiation One and Done Study (ROADS; NCT04365374) showed improved surgical-bed control with Cs-131 tiles versus post-operative stereotactic radiotherapy, but outcomes relative to pre-operative SRS are undefined. PubMed, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched through October 2026 (PRISMA 2020); one further trial was identified by other methods. Twelve-month local control (LC), leptomeningeal disease (LMD), radiation necrosis (RN), and overall survival (OS) were extracted for treatment-naïve BMs. Proportions were pooled with random-effects generalized linear mixed models and compared with a test for subgroup differences; sensitivity analyses included meta-regression, Hartung-Knapp, leave-one-out, follow-up, and fractionation analyses. Fifteen pre-operative SRS studies (918 patients/940 BMs) and four brachytherapy studies (207 patients/217 BMs) were included. Pooled 12-month LC was 97% (95% CI 90-99) with Cs-131 brachytherapy and 90% (86-93) with pre-operative SRS (test for subgroup differences p = 0.054; meta-regression p = 0.019; Hartung-Knapp p = 0.066); among studies reporting observed counts, LC was 99% vs. 90% (p = 0.009). Within pre-operative SRS, LC was 96% after hypofractionated and 86% after single-fraction treatment (p = 0.005). LMD (9.1% vs. 5.1%) and RN (0.7% vs. 5.2%) did not differ significantly. Median OS was 15.6 months with brachytherapy (range 5.9-42.5; 11.0 months, range 5.9-20.1, excluding the ROADS estimate) and 14.4 months with pre-operative SRS (range 6.3-26.4). Both approaches achieved high LC with low rates of LMD and RN. There was a trend towards higher LC with Cs-131 brachytherapy than with pre-operative SRS (97% vs. 90%; p = 0.054), and significantly so among studies reporting observed counts (99% vs. 90%; p = 0.009). Hypofractionated pre-operative SRS achieved LC similar to that of brachytherapy, suggesting that the difference may reflect single-fraction dose de-escalation rather than an intrinsic advantage of either modality. The two techniques may serve complementary roles, and prospective comparative study is warranted. This review was not registered in PROSPERO.

title: Comprehensive Outcomes From Real-World Evidence for Vagus Nerve Stimulation Therapy: Seizure and Nonseizure 36-Month Outcomes in People With Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) affects approximately one-third of all people with epilepsy and carries a disproportionate comorbidity burden. Many people with DRE are not candidates for, or do not want, resective surgery or disconnection procedures; therefore, vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) can be used for treatment. Despite its long-standing use, there is a notable lack of data regarding the newer generations of VNS Therapy devices. This study provides long-term, real-world data on the outcomes of contemporary responsive VNS Therapy devices. Comprehensive Outcomes From Real-World Evidence for VNS Therapy (CORE-VNS; NCT03529045) is a large, international, observational, prospective study designed to systematically and comprehensively evaluate the clinical and safety outcomes of people with DRE who receive a contemporary VNS system as part of their treatment plan. We report seizure, nonseizure, and safety outcomes data for participants who received their first VNS Therapy implant with at least 36 months of follow-up postimplantation. Initial implantation of the VNS Therapy System was performed in 531 participants, and 426 (80.2%) completed the study. Monthly seizure frequency for combined and individual seizure types was significantly reduced from baseline by the first three-month visit (p < 0.0001) and continued to improve throughout the study. At 36 months, the median percentage change in seizure frequency for all seizures reported at baseline was -76.3% (95% CI -83.33% to -66.67%, p < 0.0001), and 27.6% (n = 108/392; 95% CI 23.9% to 31.5%) of participants no longer reported baseline seizure types. Seizure freedom from all seizures reported during the study was achieved in 16.3% (n = 64/392; 95% CI 13.3% to 19.7%) of participants at the 36-month study visit. Results of the CORE-VNS study indicate that contemporary VNS Therapy was associated with an early and sustained benefit on seizures in participants with DRE. This reinforces adjunctive VNS Therapy as an important therapeutic option for those who cannot undergo resective surgery or disconnection procedures.

title: Closed-Loop Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Poststroke Motor Recovery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Movement-Synchronized Neuromodulation.
journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
abstract: Closed-loop or movement-synchronized vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory strategy to enhance activity-dependent neuroplasticity after stroke. Unlike conventional open-loop stimulation, closed-loop VNS is temporally coupled with motor execution, potentially improving the specificity and efficacy of motor recovery. However, clinical evidence remains fragmented, and no prior meta-analysis has specifically evaluated this approach. This study aimed to systematically assess the effectiveness and safety of closed-loop VNS for upper-limb motor recovery after stroke. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Electronic data bases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science) were searched from inception to March 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating movement-synchronized VNS in adult patients with a clinical diagnosis of stroke presenting with upper limb motor impairment were included. Primary outcomes were changes in Fugl-Meyer Assessment of Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) and Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT). Data were pooled using a random-effects model, and effect sizes were expressed as mean difference (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% CI. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Six RCTs comprising 215 participants were included in the quantitative synthesis, with an additional cohort study included qualitatively. Closed-loop VNS demonstrated a significant improvement in FMA-UE scores compared with controls (MD = 2.33, 95% CI 0.95-3.70, p = 0.0009), although with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 89%). WMFT outcomes from four RCTs (n ≈ 177) also favored closed-loop VNS (SMD = 0.62, 95% CI 0.25-0.98, p = 0.0009) with low heterogeneity (I2 = 18%). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the stability of the findings, whereas meta-regression showed no significant effect of age. The pooled adverse-event analysis of two implanted VNS trials showed no statistically significant between-group difference, although estimates were highly imprecise. Overall certainty of evidence was moderate. Closed-loop or movement-synchronized VNS may provide clinically meaningful improvements in upper-limb motor function after stroke; however, the available safety evidence is limited and imprecise, particularly for implanted VNS, and cannot be generalized to noninvasive transcutaneous auricular VNS.

title: Clinical features of the postictal state in adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional survey.
abstract: Persons with epilepsy may experience many postictal symptoms after a seizure, which can significantly impact quality of life. We aimed to determine the frequency, duration, and severity of postictal symptoms to better characterize the postictal period. Our cross-sectional questionnaire was adapted from a prior pediatric postictal survey. Face and content validity were evaluated by epilepsy experts and patients from the Calgary Epilepsy Program (CEP). The survey was pilot tested and modified, consisting of 14 physical, cognitive, and psychiatric postictal signs and symptoms. Consecutive CEP adults who had agreed to participate in research and experienced a seizure in the prior 2 years were approached. CEP clinical data were used to supplement survey data. Frequency of factors alleviating and exacerbating postictal symptoms were examined. Spearman's rho was used to explore associations between survey and CEP registry data with statistical significance at ≤ 0.05. Of 351 patients approached, 313 agreed to participate (89%). Fourteen were lost after consent was obtained, and 15 were excluded (incomplete surveys, missing registry data, not having epilepsy). Of the 298 final participants, 54% were female, mean age was 40 years (SD = 15.6), and 95% (282/298) experienced at least one postictal symptom. The three most frequent postictal symptoms were fatigue, sleepiness, or tiredness (84%), confusion or difficulty thinking clearly (75%), and memory problems (69%). For eight of 14 captured postictal symptoms, the most frequently reported symptom duration was <5 min. Mean postictal symptom burden score was correlated with patient reported quality of life and epilepsy-related disability measures. Sleep or rest, medication, and food or drinks were the most common alleviating factors. Lack of rest or sleep, and stress most often exacerbated postictal symptoms. This work contributes toward a better understanding of the postictal period and informs the development of future interventions to minimize the impact of the postictal period in epilepsy.

title: Craniofacial, Oral and Maxillofacial, and Otorhinolaryngological Injuries During the 2023-2025 War on Gaza.
abstract: The escalation of the Israeli military invasion of Gaza since October 2023 has generated an extraordinary burden of craniomaxillofacial and otorhinolaryngologic trauma while simultaneously dismantling the health system required to meet such needs. We present a purposively sampled, multi-institutional narrative case series of 22 patients managed between 2023 and 2025 in hospitals across Gaza. These lived experiences, stories, and clinical insights highlight the effect that a crumbling civilian and health infrastructure, limited access to basic medical supplies, and the indiscriminate nature of blast and gunshot wounds have on the recovery and care planning of complex pathologies. Mandibular and midface comminution, contaminated soft-tissue loss, and otologic or neurovascular injury were often present. Assessing strategies to maintain an airway, manage debridement, control hemorrhage, provide provisional fixation, and facilitate a staged return were often salient considerations when providing clinical care.

title: AI-Driven Discovery Pipeline Identifies Carvedilol as a Novel Partial Agonist of THRβ.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
abstract: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRβ) is a key therapeutic target for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and dyslipidemia, yet the discovery of structurally diverse agonists remains challenging. Here, we developed an AI-driven hierarchical drug discovery framework integrating graph neural network (GNN)-based virtual screening, structure-based modeling, and multilevel biological validation to accelerate THRβ agonist identification. The optimized GNN model outperformed conventional machine-learning approaches and enabled efficient prioritization of active compounds from an in-house library. Subsequent molecular docking and MM/GBSA rescoring identified Carvedilol as a high-confidence candidate. TR-FRET assays confirmed that Carvedilol acts as a partial THRβ agonist with preferential SRC2-2 coactivator recruitment, comparable to Resmetirom. Cellular assays further demonstrated that Carvedilol significantly reduced lipid accumulation and triglyceride levels and upregulated key metabolic regulators, including DIO1, ME1, and LDLR. Molecular dynamics and dcTMD analyses elucidated that Carvedilol is stabilized within the ligand-binding pocket through dominant hydrophobic interactions and specific hydrogen bonds with Thr273 and His435. Overall, this study repurposes Carvedilol as a structurally distinct THRβ agonist and validates an effective AI-guided strategy for nuclear receptor-targeted drug discovery.

title: Senescence-Associated Loss of α-Synuclein in Brain Microvascular Endothelium Compromises Tight Junctions and Disrupts Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity.
abstract: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is an early feature of brain aging, but the endothelial mechanisms preserving barrier resilience remain unclear. Although we have reported α-synuclein (SNCA) supports vascular endothelial homeostasis, its role in the brain microvascular endothelium is unknown. Because SNCA loss suppresses eNOS/NO signaling and promotes endothelial β-site amyloid precursor protein cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) induction, we investigated whether senescence-associated SNCA decline drives BACE1-dependent BBB injury. Replicative senescence in human brain microvascular endothelial cells (HBMECs) reduced SNCA expression. siRNA-mediated SNCA depletion induced a senescence-like state with increased β-galactosidase activity, CDKN2A/p16 and TP53/p53 induction, and decreased SIRT1, eNOS, and glypican-1. SNCA-deficient HBMECs showed impaired proliferation and migration, loss of occludin and ZO-1, increased permeability, and elevated BACE1 expression and activity; BACE1 co-silencing restored junctional proteins and normalized permeability. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling excluded most classical BACE1-regulatory mechanisms and instead implicated coordinated disruption of the NO-sGC-cGMP axis, consistent with the partial rescue by the NO donor SNAP. Amyloid-β42 oligomers sensitized SNCA-deficient monolayers to barrier injury at concentrations that left control monolayers unaffected. Global SNCA-knockout mice exhibited multiregional BBB leakage, reduced occludin, ZO-1, and claudin-5, and p53 immunoreactivity confined to CD31-positive microvessels. This phenotype was present in young adulthood and was reproduced in aged wild-type mice, which showed reduced SNCA in isolated brain microvessels. These findings identify senescence-associated endothelial SNCA loss as a candidate contributor to brain microvascular barrier vulnerability, describing an endothelial stress pathway in which SNCA insufficiency is associated with BACE1-dependent tight junction destabilization in the aging brain.

title: Assessing Treatment Response in Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus: A Prospective Comparison of Outcome Measures.
abstract: Assessment of treatment response in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) lacks a universally accepted standardized outcome measure. Therefore, this study compared the disease-specific Gothenburg scale (GBS), the GBS without gait velocity, the modified Rankin Scale, the iNPH Grading Scale, and the 15-dimensonal health-related quality-of-life instrument against gait speed improvement to evaluate the responsiveness and discriminative ability of the GBS during a 12-month postshunting follow-up. This was a prospective population-based cohort study in which patients undergoing shunt surgery were evaluated preoperatively and up to 36 months postoperatively. The primary analyses included the preoperative assessments and assessments at 3 and 12 months after shunt surgery. Responsiveness was measured using the standardized response mean (SRM), and the discriminative ability to detect gait speed improvement was analyzed using the area under the curve (AUC). The GBS was the most responsive and stable scale: SRM values 0.80 (95% CI, 0.67-0.93) at 3 months and 0.72 (95% CI, 0.57-0.87) at 12 months. Using the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) as the anchor, the corresponding AUCs were 0.85 (95% CI, 0.81-0.90) and 0.91 (95% CI, 0.86-0.95). The GBS without gait velocity showed similar performance with SRMs of 0.76 (95% CI, 0.63-0.88) and 0.68 (95% CI, 0.53-0.82) and AUCs of 0.82 (95% CI, 0.77-0.87) and 0.87 (95% CI, 0.82-0.93) at 3 and 12 months. The 15D showed the lowest responsiveness, failing to capture disease-specific changes. The GBS is a strong and highly sensitive scale for monitoring patients with iNPH. General and non-disease-specific outcome measures should only be used as complementary indicators accompanied by gait speed evaluations.

title: Continuous and Segmental Cervical Ossification of the Posterior Longitudinal Ligament Have Distinct Genomic Architectures: Inflammatory Versus Bone Metabolic Phenotypes on Whole-Exome Sequencing.
abstract: Cervical ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) may represent 2 convergent entities-a genetically driven continuous phenotype and an idiopathic segmental phenotype-with a wide clinical prognosis ranging from asymptomatic to life-threatening quadriplegia. However, previous studies evaluated OPLL as a single homogeneous entity, leaving subtype-specific mechanisms unresolved. We sought to delineate the genomic, biomarker, and clinical determinants distinguishing continuous from segmental OPLL. Patients diagnosed with cervical OPLL and healthy controls were consecutively enrolled between March 2021 and February 2024. All participants underwent whole-exome sequencing, radiological examinations, and blood biomarker measurements (C-reactive protein [CRP], white blood cell, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, alkaline phosphatase, and osteocalcin). To maximize phenotypic homogeneity, subgroups were defined by K-means clustering (occupying ratio and progression rate). Single-variant and gene-wise variant burden analyses were performed. In total, 176 participants were enrolled: 52 with continuous/mixed OPLL (Group C), 58 with segmental/localized OPLL (Group S), and 66 OPLL-free controls (Group N). Clustering identified a severe continuous subgroup (n = 31) and a mild segmental subgroup (n = 45). Group C was significantly younger and exhibited greater ossification depth, length, and occupying ratio; faster progression; and higher white blood cell count and CRP level than Group S; the annual progression rate correlated positively with CRP (r = 0.208, P = .035). Gene-wise analysis associated the severe subgroup C with immune- and oxidative stress-related genes (KIR2DL3, OGG1), OR2T6, and ZAR1 relative to controls, whereas CCDC154, a bone metabolism gene, uniquely distinguished the segmental phenotype and displayed a graded burden that increased sequentially from the severe continuous to the milder segmental subgroups. Continuous and segmental OPLL exhibit distinct genomic architectures-an inflammatory phenotype (KIR2DL3, OGG1) vs a bone metabolic phenotype (CCDC154). This multimodal subtyping may support a mechanism-based reclassification of OPLL and guide patient-specific prognostication.

title: Behavioral Determinants of Adult Hearing Health Care Engagement Across the Care Pathway: A Scoping Review Using the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior Framework.
journal: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
abstract: The aim of this study was to identify behavioral determinants influencing adult hearing health care engagement across the hearing health care pathway and to map these determinants to the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) framework. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Electronic searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, CINAHL, and Web of Science identified 767 records. Fourteen studies involving adults with hearing loss or hearing difficulties met inclusion criteria. Determinants were identified across multiple stages of the hearing health care pathway, revealing stage-specific behavioral influences and evidence gaps across the engagement continuum. Determinants were mapped to the six domains of the COM-B framework. Reflective motivation was represented in all included studies, while social opportunity, physical opportunity, and psychological capability were also frequently reported. Evidence was concentrated at the treatment adoption stage, with comparatively limited research addressing earlier pathway stages or longitudinal behavioral transitions. Adult hearing health care engagement is shaped by interacting motivational, social, capability-related, and structural determinants across the care pathway. A COM-B-informed synthesis provides a behavioral framework for understanding where engagement may break down and for guiding stage-specific interventions to improve help-seeking, treatment uptake, and sustained engagement with hearing technologies. https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34930449.

title: Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons.
abstract: Sensory neurons are traditionally viewed as feature detectors that respond with an increase in firing rate to preferred stimuli while remaining unresponsive to others. Here, we identify a dual-feature encoding strategy in macaque visual cortex, wherein many neurons in areas V1 and V4 are selectively tuned to two distinct visual features-one that enhances and one that suppresses activity-around an elevated baseline firing rate. By combining neuronal recordings with functional digital twin models-deep learning-based predictive models of biological neurons-we were able to systematically identify each neuron's preferred and non-preferred features. These feature pairs served as anchors for a continuous, low-dimensional axis in natural image similarity space, along which neuronal activity varied approximately linearly. Within a single visual area, visual features that strongly or weakly activated individual neurons also had a high probability of modulating the activity of other neurons, suggesting a shared feature selectivity across the population that structures stimulus encoding. We show that this encoding strategy is conserved across species, present in both primary and lateral visual areas of mouse cortex. Dual-feature selectivity is consistent with recent anatomical evidence for feature-specific inhibitory connectivity, complementing the feature-detector principle through circuit mechanisms in which selective excitation and inhibition may together enhance the representational capacity of the neuronal population.

title: Prevalence and ultrasonographic characterization of newly detected findings suggestive of deep and ovarian endometriosis in postmenopausal women undergoing routine gynecological examination.
abstract: To assess the prevalence and ultrasonographic characteristics of newly detected findings suggestive of ovarian and deep endometriosis (DE) in postmenopausal women undergoing routine gynecological evaluation. This prospective observational study (NCT07503938) included consecutive postmenopausal participants attending two regional gynecology outpatient clinics for routine examination over 24 months. Transvaginal ultrasound was performed by a single operator according to International Deep Endometriosis Analysis (IDEA) group criteria. Findings suggestive of DE and/or ovarian cysts suggestive of endometriomas were recorded and characterized. Clinical data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with posterior compartment hypoechoic nodules. Four hundred ninety-two participants were included (mean age 60.2 ± 6.1 years; median time since menopause 8.0 years). Ultrasound findings suggestive of endometriosis were identified in 40 participants (8.1%; 95% CI 5.9%-10.9%), including posterior compartment hypoechoic nodules in 36 (7.3%). Intestinal nodules (n = 21; 4.3%) often showed plaque-like morphology, thickness 10 years; p for trend = 0.001). In multivariable analysis, ≤5 years since menopause was independently associated with posterior nodules (adjusted OR 3.25, 95% CI 1.35-7.83), as were a history of dysmenorrhea (adjusted OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.05-4.60) and chronic pelvic pain (adjusted OR 2.36, 95% CI 1.11-5.00). No independent association was observed with current pelvic pain, dyschezia, previous infertility, or systemic hormone replacement therapy. Six ovarian cysts with ultrasonographic features suggestive of endometriomas were identified (1.2%; 95% CI 0.45%-2.64%), five of which exhibited atypical features, including multilocularity, heterogeneous echoes, papillary excrescences, or wall thickening. Ultrasound findings suggestive of DE may be detected after menopause and are associated with earlier postmenopausal timing and a history of reproductive-age pain, but not with specific current pain symptoms or hormonal exposure. Their predominantly plaque-like, poorly vascularized morphology may reflect fibrotic remodeling, although histological composition and biological activity cannot be established by ultrasound alone. Expert ultrasound remains important to distinguish benign-appearing residual findings from clinically relevant or malignant pathology.

title: Gait Adaptability Rehabilitation: Perspectives From Individuals With Motor Incomplete Spinal Cord Injury.
journal: Journal of neurologic physical therapy : JNPT
abstract: Following motor incomplete spinal cord injury (SCI), gait adaptability, which is the ability to modify one's gait pattern in response to task/environmental demands, is likely impaired. Despite rehabilitation, many individuals with motor incomplete SCI face ongoing walking challenges and view safe walking as an unmet goal. This study explored the perceived importance and appropriateness of addressing gait adaptability during SCI rehabilitation from the perspectives of community-dwelling adults with subacute, motor incomplete SCI. A qualitative study using semi-structured interviews was conducted. The interview guide was structured around the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) model, which examines the physical, social, and psychological factors influencing behavior. Questions queried participants' perspectives on current rehabilitation practices aimed at improving gait adaptability. Interviews were conducted 3 to 6 months post-inpatient discharge, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using interpretive description. Fourteen individuals with motor incomplete SCI who completed walking training in inpatient rehabilitation were interviewed (9 males/men, 5 females/women). Three themes highlighting participant perceptions were identified: (1) gait adaptability is important for community reintegration, (2) perceived gait adaptability training and assessment practices: training is variable, with progress commonly measured by distance, and (3) real-world walking is complex: Training should reflect where people walk. Each theme included 2 subthemes, with participants highlighting the importance of real-world walking exposure, outdoor practice, and the role of personal goals in driving motivation. This study highlights the perceived importance of gait adaptability training for individuals with motor incomplete SCI, emphasizing its role in fostering confidence and independence post-inpatient discharge.

title: Limited Passive Diffusion of Apolipoprotein E Across the Human Blood-CSF Barrier: Evidence From Paired CSF/Serum Quotients.
abstract: Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) is a major genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease and a potential therapeutic target, but the relative contribution of peripheral blood-derived and intrathecally synthesized ApoE to the CNS remains unclear. A novel electrophoresis-based capillary Western blot assay was validated to quantify Pan-ApoE and ApoE4 in paired human CSF and serum samples (n = 34), followed by analysis of CSF/serum quotients. Serum ApoE concentrations were ninefold higher than CSF concentrations, with CSF/serum quotients of 0.132 for Pan-ApoE and 0.191 for ApoE4. Compared with theoretical quotients predicted for proteins entering CSF solely by passive diffusion according to their hydrodynamic radius according to Felgenhauer et al., the observed quotients were 66- to 1320-fold higher for Pan-ApoE and 96- to 1910-fold higher for ApoE4. Based on this model, passive diffusion was estimated to account for less than 1.5% of CSF ApoE. These estimates are model-dependent and may vary with ApoE isoform and extent of lipidation, which could potentially be affected by serum fibrin clot formation. The remaining ApoE fraction (> 98.5%) may reflect active transport, intrathecal synthesis or both. Pan-ApoE and ApoE4 CSF/serum quotients lacked statistically significant association with CSF/serum albumin quotient as a marker of blood-CSF barrier function. Both quotients also exceeded the values predicted by a theoretical reference curve relating CSF/serum protein quotients to the albumin quotient, adapted from the Reiber model using immunoglobulin G parameters based on the comparable hydrodynamic radii of IgG and ApoE.

title: Neural Correlates of Smoking Cessation: A Systematic Review of Magnetic Resonance Imaging Studies.
journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
abstract: Tobacco use is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite efficacious interventions, smoking cessation remains difficult for many individuals. While demographic and behavioural predictors of smoking cessation outcomes are well-documented, neurobiological predictors of success have been inconsistent across studies. The current systematic review aimed to identify neuroimaging biomarkers consistently associated with smoking cessation success. A systematic search identified 32 studies that examined neural predictors of outcomes across structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging modalities and intervention types. The most frequently implicated brain regions included the medial prefrontal cortex (PFC), striatum, and anterior insula. Specifically, greater medial PFC response to health promotion tasks; greater reactivity to smoking-related cues in the dorsolateral PFC and dorsal striatum; stronger resting state functional connectivity between the insula and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, precuneus, and medial frontal gyrus; and greater global gray matter volume were commonly reported as predictors of better treatment response. The current systematic review identifies the most robust MRI biomarkers of smoking cessation, but in a relatively small overall literature with extensive heterogeneity among studies.

title: Virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight performance are mediated by the octopamine pathway.
abstract: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. In insects, the octopamine (OA) pathway orchestrates the 'fight-or-flight' response, regulating energy mobilization, temperature, and flight. We determined that sacbrood virus (SBV) infections induce expression of an OA receptor and enhance honey flight performance, whereas deformed wing virus (DWV) infections reduce flight performance, but how viruses interface with this pathway remained unknown. To elucidate the relationships between the OA response, virus infection, and flight, honey bees were infected with SBV or DWV and exposed to OA, epinastine (EP) - an OA receptor antagonist, or both OA and EP; flight and gene expression were assessed. Pharmacologic manipulation revealed that OA supplementation rescued flight deficits in DWV-infected bees, but diminished performance in SBV-infected bees, while blocking OA receptors altered these effects. Transcriptome analyses indicated that SBV infections, and DWV infection with OA treatment, activated honey bee metabolic pathways, and that SBV-infected bees had greater expression of genes involved in OA synthesis, unless treated with OA. These results provide mechanistic insight for virus-specific impacts on honey bee flight, which may have consequences for foraging efficiency, colony health, and virus transmission.

title: What can functional transcranial Doppler ultrasonography reveal about the cerebral lateralization of writing.
abstract: Written language is central to modern life, yet its cerebral lateralization remains far less understood than that of oral language. This review synthesizes evidence from five functional transcranial Doppler ultrasonography (fTCD) studies (n = 268; 228 adults and 40 children aged 7-9 years), a method well-suited to studying writing due to its tolerance of natural movement. The linguistic component of writing has been shown to be left-lateralized in right-handers, mirroring oral language, whereas for left-handers findings remain inconclusive. Linguistic processing appears largely independent of whether words are produced by hand or keyboard. The unresolved issue is dissociating linguistic from motor components as writing movements may themselves be intrinsically linguistic. Future research should address underexplored populations and leverage writing as a model for neuroplasticity.

title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
abstract: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups. Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

title: Evidence of high rates of burnout symptoms in a cohort with cluster headache.
abstract: Cluster headache is a debilitating primary headache disorder. During active bouts, headache attacks occur daily and can last up to 3 h. Besides the excruciating pain, the disorder can greatly impact a patient's mental health, sleep, and life quality. The reoccurring attacks as well as sleep problems may lead to energy depletion and burnout symptoms, which can limit a person's ability to participate in society to the extent they would like to. Our aim was to investigate the extent of burnout symptoms in a Swedish cluster headache cohort using a cross-sectional approach. We further wanted to study if burnout symptoms can be linked to disease status-and if sex, lifestyle factors, or any specific clinical characteristics may be linked to change in burnout symptoms. Between January 2024 and September 2025, the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire was sent out via the Research Electronic Data Capture platform to 839 study participants with cluster headache. Global scores from the questionnaire were compared between study participants in active bout and remission. Likewise, the scores were analyzed between participants whose remission period had lasted longer than 5 years (long-term) compared to less than 5 years (short-term). Lifestyle and clinical factors were further analyzed in study participants with high Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire scores (global score >3.75). The total number of individuals included in the analysis was 373/839 (44.5%). Scores above threshold (>3.75) were recorded in 65.9% (58/88) of study participants in an active bout compared to 37.5% (90/240) in the remission group (odds ratio [OR] = 3.22, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.93-5.38; p < 0.001). Participants in short-term remission similarly had a higher percentage of scores above threshold compared to participants in long-term remission (42.0% [73/174] vs. 22.2% [12/54], OR = 2.53, 95% CI = 1.25-5.14; p = 0.009). Participants with burnout scores above 3.75 were more likely to be females (OR = 3.25, 95% CI = 2.04-5.19; pcorrected <0.001) and report sleep deprivation as an attack trigger (OR = 2.24, 95% CI = 1.32-3.82; pcorrected = 0.034). Participants with cluster headache in our Swedish cohort reported higher scores for burnout symptoms, particularly during active bout. For participants in remission, the burnout symptoms score was inversely correlated to the number of years since their last active headache bout. When managing cluster headache in a clinical setting, it should be taken into consideration that this patient group has a substantial risk for developing burnout symptoms both in and out of an active bout. Future studies should evaluate how to best support patients with cluster headache handling exhaustion and promote recovery to improve their quality of life.

title: Histopathologic Considerations for Indication of Cochlear Implant for Patients With Vestibular Schwannoma.
journal: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
abstract: Predicting cochlear implant (CI) outcomes in patients with vestibular schwannoma (VS) is challenging, even when the cochlear nerve remains anatomically intact. This study examined how cochlear and neural pathology relate to premortem audiometric findings, pure-tone average (PTA) and speech discrimination score (SDS), to explore histopathologic conditions that may be relevant to CI candidacy. Temporal bones labeled as "acoustic neuroma" were selected from the House Ear Institute Temporal Bone Registry. Twenty-eight patients (34 ears) with well-preserved cochlear structures were included. Clinical data, including audiometry, surgical history, and surgical approach, were reviewed. Histologic analysis assessed residual tumor, fundal involvement, and the status of cochlear hair cells and spiral ganglion cells (SGCs). Pathology was correlated with clinical and audiometric features. Among 34 specimens from 28 patients, 7 were from nonsurgical cases and 27 from surgical cases. In cases with preserved hearing (PTA ≤60 dB or SDS ≥60%), spiral ganglion cell (SGC) counts exceeded 20,000, and hair cells were well preserved. Cases with severe PTA elevation commonly showed hair cell injury, yet SGCs remained partially preserved. In contrast, reduced SDS was consistently associated with SGC loss. After a translabyrinthine approach, SGCs and hair cells were nearly absent within 3 to 27 months in most cases, and cochlear ossification was observed in cases surviving beyond 50 months. In all cases with tumor extension into the fundus of the internal auditory canal, hearing was completely lost, and both hair cells and SGCs showed severe degeneration. SDS may parallel SGC status in VS, possibly more closely than PTA. These findings suggest that early tumor removal before fundal extension and preservation of the cochlear nerve may be associated with cochlear and neural integrity, which could be relevant for future CI candidacy.

title: [The connotation and application thoughts of brain-reproductive medicine].
journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
abstract: Neuroscience is a scientific discipline that meticulously dissects the architecture and functionality of the brain, as well as the physiological and pathological mechanisms of the nervous system. Reproductive medicine, on the other hand, is a specialized field that concentrates on scrutinizing the physiological and pathological processes within the male and female reproductive systems. The brain and the reproductive system are reciprocally intertwined in both structural and functional aspects, synergistically sustaining human growth, development, and procreation. Their relationship is conventionally encapsulated and explicated by the hypothalamus-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis. However, additional nexuses independent of this axis also prevail between the brain and the reproductive system.In the female context, the brain exerts its modulatory influence on reproductive function through neurotransmitter-mediated signaling and neurotrophic factor-dependent pathways. Reproductive hormones, in turn, can modulate neurotrophic factors to confer neuroprotection and perturb cerebral hemodynamics and white matter integrity. In the male counterpart, the brain impacts reproductive function via neurotransmitter-mediated transduction, and its anatomical conformation can directly impinge on male reproductive capabilities. Reproductive hormones can also influence the brain by means of antioxidant stress mitigation and anti-inflammatory responses.The aggregate of these brain-reproductive interaction mechanisms, in conjunction with the HPG axis, delineate the highly convoluted and multifaceted relationship between the brain and the reproductive system. Grounded on the cutting-edge research and oriented towards theoretical deliberations and clinical exigencies, the concept of "brain reproductive medicine" is cogently postulated. This concept zeroes in on the exploration of the complex relationship between the brain and reproduction, serving as a referential framework for disciplinary progression and academic interchange, augmenting the profundity of understanding regarding the brain-reproductive system relationship, and potentiating the caliber of multidisciplinary therapeutics for affiliated maladies.

title: Anterior Middle Cingulate Cortex Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Level Is Elevated in Children With Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder With and Without Prenatal Alcohol Exposure.
abstract: Prior neuroimaging suggests brain differences between children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and prenatal alcohol exposure (ADHD+PAE) and non-exposed children with ADHD due to non-PAE causes (ADHD-PAE). There has been interest in regional brain levels of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glutamate (Glu) measured in vivo with magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) as possible indicators of local inhibitory, respectively, excitatory activity in ADHD. For the first time, we report here a comparison of GABA and Glu in ADHD+PAE vs. ADHD-PAE. At 3 Tesla, we used J-difference-edited single-voxel MRS to assay GABA and Glu in 27 children with ADHD+PAE, 21 with ADHD-PAE, and 28 typically developing (TD) controls, all aged between 7 and 14 years. MRS was sampled from midline anterior middle cingulate cortex (aMCC), the "cognitive cingulate" considered functionally relevant to ADHD. Spectra were fit with custom software, including a unique technique for isolating the GABA signal from the confounding macromolecular baseline (MMBL). aMCC GABA was higher in ADHD+PAE and ADHD-PAE than in TD. GABA increased with age in TD, but not in ADHD+PAE or ADHD-PAE. Similar effects were observed for the ratios GABA/Glu and GABA/Glx. For GABA+MMBL (GABA+) these effects were not seen; rather, GABA+ and MMBL increased with age for the ADHD+PAE group only. No significant effects were found for Glu or Glx. GABA in the aMCC does not distinguish the two etiologies of ADHD; rather, elevated GABA that follows an abnormal development appears to be common to both. High GABA may reflect increased inhibition of the aMCC impairing its cognitive functions. GABA+ results in ADHD may not track reliably with underlying GABA values. Negative results for Glu and Glx should be reexamined at shorter echo-times.

title: [Therapeutic advances of tadalafil in multi-organ systemic diseases beyond erectile dysfunction].
journal: Zhonghua nan ke xue = National journal of andrology
abstract: Phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) participates in the physiological functions of multiple organs by regulating the nitric oxide (NO)-cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) pathway. As a long-acting PDE5 inhibitor, tadalafil has been used clinically for over 20 years and is approved for the treatment of male erectile dysfunction and lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia. Furthermore, tadalafil maintains cGMP levels by inhibiting PDE5, thereby activating the downstream NO-cGMP signaling pathway to exert multiple effects, including relaxing smooth muscle, exerting antioxidant actions, regulating apoptosis, and modulating metabolism. Clinical evidence indicates that tadalafil shows promising therapeutic potential in multi-organ system diseases such as pulmonary arterial hypertension, heart failure, type 2 diabetes, cognitive impairment, female infertility, and fetal growth restriction. This article systematically reviews the action mechanisms and research progress of tadalafil in treating diseases beyond erectile dysfunction, aiming to summarize its potential for cross-disease system clinical applications and provide references for optimizing treatment strategies for patients with chronic diseases.

title: Prevalence and correlates of daily cannabis use in Great Britain in 2023-2024: Results from a nationally representative cross-sectional survey.
abstract: Cannabis health harms increase as use increases, but little is known about who is more likely to use frequently. In England and Wales in 2025, it was estimated that 470 000 adults used cannabis daily. We aimed to provide an estimate for Great Britain, and to examine associations between daily use and socio-demographic characteristics, mental health and nicotine use variables. Pooled data from repeat cross-sectional national online surveys (Action on Smoking and Health) fielded in February-March 2023 and 2024. Great Britain. Adults aged ≥18 years (n = 25 537). Self-reported past-year and daily cannabis use prevalence. Correlates of daily use were assessed using stepwise quasi-Poisson regression models. Prevalence of past-year cannabis consumption was 7.2% (n = 1882) and, of these, 24.2% (n = 432) reported daily cannabis use. Factors associated with increased risk of daily cannabis use included being older than 24 [25-35 years adjusted risk ratio (aRR) = 1.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.16-2.21; 35-44 years aRR = 2.09, 95% CI = 1.53-2.84; 45-54 years aRR = 2.03, 95% CI = 1.46-2.83; 55 + years aRR = 1.76, 95% CI = 1.23-2.53]; being unemployed (aRR = 1.34, 95% CI = 1.12-1.61); currently smoking tobacco (aRR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.51-2.18) and using a combustible route of cannabis administration (aRR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.26-2.08). Gender, ethnicity, region, social grade, anxiety or depression were not associated with daily use. In Great Britain, 1.2 million people are estimated to be using cannabis daily. Daily cannabis use is more common among people who are older, are less advantaged and smoke tobacco.

title: Reactive Astrocyte-Associated IL-33 Signaling Contributes to a Protective Neuroimmune State During Chronic Toxoplasma gondii-Plasmodium berghei Coinfection.
abstract: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a lethal neuroinflammatory syndrome characterized by blood-brain barrier disruption and excessive immune-mediated neuronal damage. Astrocytes are emerging as key regulators of CNS homeostasis, yet their contribution to disease tolerance during polymicrobial infections remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chronic Toxoplasma gondii (Tg) infection protects against experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) induced by Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA) by establishing a regulated neuroimmune environment rather than reducing cerebral parasite burden. This protective phenotype required chronic cerebral T. gondii infection and was associated with a distinct neuroinflammatory transcriptional profile characterized by enhanced TGF-β and IL-33/ST2 expression. At the cellular level, chronic Tg infection remodeled the astrocyte compartment, generating reactive astrocytes displaying an intermediate inflammatory phenotype characterized by the co-expression of inflammatory (CXCL-10, MHC-I) and regulatory (TGF-β) markers. Reactive astrocytes represented one of the major IL-33-expressing cell populations in the brains of Tg-infected and coinfected mice and were associated with recruitment of ST2-expressing group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s), which expressed IL-5 and IL-13 in the brain. In IL-33-deficient mice, cerebral ILC2 recruitment was markedly reduced and protection against ECM was only partially maintained, indicating that the IL-33/ST2 axis contributes to, but is not solely responsible for, disease tolerance during coinfection. Our findings identify reactive astrocytes as key components of a regulated neuroimmune environment associated with protection against ECM during chronic T. gondii coinfection. These results highlight astrocyte-associated IL-33/ST2 signaling and ILC2 recruitment as components of a multicellular neuroimmune network that contribute to disease tolerance during polymicrobial CNS infections.

title: Plcg2 Deficiency Leads to Sex-Associated Divergent Effects on Glial Transcriptomes.
abstract: Plcg2 encodes an intracellular phospholipase C signaling enzyme expressed predominately in microglia in the brain. Genome-wide association studies implicate PLCG2 in Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk and loss of Plcg2 alters amyloid pathology in mouse models. However, the physiological impact of Plcg2 loss remains unclear. To address this gap, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous Plcg2-deficient mouse brains in the absence of amyloid or tau pathology. Our analyses generated a comprehensive, publicly available atlas of glial transcriptomic states across genotypes and sexes. Genotype-associated changes in microglia and astrocytes were enriched in neurodegenerative disease-related pathways, as well as oxidative phosphorylation and proteostasis pathways. Genotype-by-sex interaction and sex-stratified analyses revealed divergent regulation of many of these pathways in males and females, while co-expression and cell-cell communication analyses identified additional sex-associated differences in glial signaling networks. Overall, these data provide a framework for understanding how variation in PLCG2 function may shape glial biology and modify pathways relevant to neurodegenerative disease in a sex-associated manner.

title: Delivery of atropine complexed with hydroxypropyl beta-cyclodextrin via a contact lens.
journal: Optometry and vision science : official publication of the American Academy of Optometry
abstract: Myopia is a global vision problem linked to a significant economic burden and potential blindness in severe cases. Current interventions-including atropine eye drops, contact lenses, spectacles, and lifestyle changes-are often combined due to limited individual effectiveness. This study aimed to develop and stabilize atropine formulations, load them into contact lenses, and evaluate atropine release profiles. Atropine sulfate was converted to atropine base and complexed with 2-hydroxypropyl beta-cyclodextrin (HPBCD) in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) at pH 6.5 or 7.4. Formulation stability was monitored over one year at room temperature (21°C) using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Etafilcon A and omafilcon A lenses were soaked in the formulations for 24 hours. The amount of atropine base loaded and released was quantified via HPLC, and toxicity was assessed according to ISO 10993-5. After 1 year, the formulations retained 97.3% (pH 6.5) and 80.3% (pH 7.4) of atropine base. At pH 6.5, etafilcon A and omafilcon A absorbed 3.2 ± 0.1 μg and 1.7 ± 0.6 μg of atropine base, respectively. Etafilcon A released 100% of the atropine base within 4 hours, and omafilcon A released 59% within 2 hours. Contact lens eluates showed no toxicity. These findings support the stability and safety of atropine base formulations for potential ocular drug delivery.

title: Real-world profiles and associated factors of pediatric asthma monitoring.
journal: Pediatric allergy and immunology : official publication of the European Society of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology
abstract: Achieving and maintaining pediatric asthma control depends on effective and regular monitoring. While a wide range of monitoring tools are available, how and why clinicians use these in routine practice has not been formally characterized. Here we describe distinct real-world monitoring patterns among healthcare professionals (HCPs) caring for children with asthma in an international convenience survey, examining the geographic, professional, and institutional factors associated with them. Data from the international cross-sectional Pediatric Asthma in Real Life (PeARL) HCP survey, administered to clinicians with expertise in childhood asthma, were analyzed. Monitoring patterns were derived by Ward agglomerative hierarchical clustering on four standardized domains: clinical evaluation, spirometry, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), and home-monitoring. Independent associations between cluster membership and region, specialty, sector, and level of care were estimated by multinomial logistic regression (MLR). 951 HCPs from 78 countries were included. Four monitoring patterns emerged: Low-intensity (n = 88, 9.3%), lower overall monitoring intensity but moderate clinical assessment; Clinical (n = 449, 47.2%), predominantly clinical assessment with moderate spirometry but infrequent FeNO and home monitoring; Clinical & Objective (n = 308, 32.4%) with additional regular spirometry with moderate FeNO use and Comprehensive (n = 106, 11.1%), also providing home monitoring. In MLR (n = 933), region and care level were significantly associated with cluster membership (p < .001), and specialty (p = .012) and sector (p = .039) also contributed independently. The most pronounced gradients involved objective in-clinic testing: specialists were 3.5-fold (95% CI 1.68-7.37) more likely than generalists, and tertiary-care HCPs 3.3-fold (95% CI 1.99-5.58) more likely than primary-care HCPs, to belong to the Clinical & Objective pattern, with routine use of objective measures concentrated in Western and Northern European practices. Home monitoring showed no consistent gradient across the measured characteristics. Real-world pediatric asthma monitoring follows recognizable patterns, distinguished by the use of objective in-clinic testing and between-visit home-based practices. Nearly half of HCPs relied predominantly on clinical assessment with limited use of FeNO and home-based monitoring, and only a minority integrated home-monitoring tools. Objective in-clinic testing concentrated in specialist services and Western/Northern European practices, while home-monitoring adoption showed no consistent gradient. These findings identify factors associated with pediatric asthma monitoring and suggest system-level factors that warrant direct evaluation in dedicated implementation studies.

title: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition: from LDL lowering to dementia prevention.
abstract: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors most importantly lower apoB-containing lipoproteins, yet genetic and pharmacological intervention data underscore possible benefits extending to new-onset diabetes, kidney function, septicemia and possibly dementia. To understand these sequelae, this review examines in what manner CETP inhibition reshapes lipoprotein composition, with special focus on HDL structure and function, and how these changes may underlie clinical benefits beyond consequences of LDL lowering alone. Because of its central role in lipoprotein metabolism, potent CETP inhibition leads to comprehensive lipid modulation: coordinately reducing LDL-C, apoB, non-HDL-C and Lp(a) while raising HDL-C, apoA-I, preβ1 and preβ2 HDL. Beyond these changes, it remodels HDL towards a more functional cargo-carrying particle, enriched with monomeric lipid-free apoA-I, apoE, apoM-sphingosine-1-phosphate and a host of lipophilic antioxidants. These findings offer a plausible mechanistic basis for the observed reduction in new-onset diabetes, modest attenuation of kidney-function decline, preliminary sepsis-related signals and lowering of early Alzheimer's disease markers. By simultaneously lowering apoB-lipoproteins and remodeling HDL to become more functional, CETP inhibition offers a coherent rationale for potential benefit across cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, immune and neurological disease. The currently ongoing obicetrapib cardiovascular outcomes trial will test whether clinical benefit follows this biology.

title: Self-Reported Dysphagia in Head and Neck Cancer Survivors From Diagnosis to Twelve Months Post Treatment and Predictors for Moderate to Severe Long-Term Dysphagia.
abstract: Dysphagia is a common complication of head and neck cancer (HNC) and its treatment. This study examined swallowing-related quality of life from diagnosis to 12 months after treatment, compared swallowing outcomes across tumor sites and treatment modalities, and identified predictors of moderate-to-severe dysphagia. The M. D. Anderson Dysphagia Inventory (MDADI) was completed by 445 patients receiving curatively intended HNC treatment pre-treatment and at 3-, 6-, and 12-months post-treatment. Swallowing-related quality of life worsened during treatment, the poorest scores at 3 months post-treatment; 21.6% reported moderate-to-severe dysphagia, decreasing to 12.5% at 12 months. Risk factors for dysphagia at 12 months included stage IV disease, surgery combined with (chemo)radiotherapy, smoking cessation within 12 months, and pre-treatment sick leave. Patients with cervical carcinoma of unknown primary (CCUP) had the poorest outcomes. Swallowing function declined during treatment. Patients receiving surgery combined with (chemo)radiotherapy and patients with CCUP are at increased risk of long-term dysphagia and require closer follow-up.

title: The pen-and-paper tube figures mental rotation task for patients with trauma-related disorders: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Introduction: Most patients with trauma-related disorders have intrusive memories (IMs) of trauma. Recently a new type of digital treatment (imagery-competing task intervention; ICTI) has been shown to reduce the rate of IMs and other symptoms. Here we examine a novel pen-and-paper ICTI called 'Tube figures' suitable for settings without digital resources.Methods and analysis: Forty patients with trauma-related disorders participated in a mono-centre, single-blind randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (Intervention: Tube figures ICTI vs. Control: Wikipedia). Participants selected one IM to monitor daily for four weeks. After two weeks, a single intervention or control session was administered for the monitored IM. Primary outcome was the frequency of the IM monitored per week for the two weeks following the intervention. A mixed Poisson regression was fitted with intervention and study phase (baseline/pre- and post-intervention) as fixed effects and a random effect for patient. Severity of symptoms at study start and two weeks after randomization was assessed with the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5).Results: The frequency of the monitored IM per week reduced significantly more after the intervention versus control (22% versus 2% reduction in the two weeks post-intervention compared to two weeks pre-intervention, respectively). PCL-5 score reduced significantly more after intervention (53-38) than control (55-47).Discussion: This single-session pen-and-paper Tube figures ICTI reduced IM frequency and trauma-related symptoms, consistent with digital ICTI studies. Limitations include the reliance on self-report measures and only having data for the two weeks after intervention. Future studies should explore the different components of the intervention and test practical aspects that could promote its use in low-resource settings.

title: Monoaminergic signatures of treatment-response heterogeneity in schizophrenia: a neuromelanin MRI study.
abstract: Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) provides a noninvasive measure of signal within monoaminergic nuclei, including the substantia nigra/ventral tegmental area (SN-VTA) and locus coeruleus (LC). These signals are thought to reflect long-term monoaminergic-related processes. Although presynaptic dopamine dysfunction is implicated in schizophrenia, the contribution of monoaminergic-related NM-MRI signal alterations to treatment-response heterogeneity, including clozapine nonresponse, remains unclear. We conducted a cross-sectional NM-MRI study, including patients with ultra-resistant schizophrenia (URS; n = 16), clozapine-responsive treatment-resistant schizophrenia (non-URS; n = 16), first-line antipsychotic responders (FLR; n = 20), and healthy controls (HCs; n = 26). NM-MRI contrast ratios (CR) were quantified in the SN-VTA and LC. Group differences were assessed using covariate-adjusted models, and voxel-wise analyses were performed to localize SN-VTA effects.
