SN-VTA CR was higher in both URS (d = 1.01) and FLR (d = 0.94) than in HCs, with voxel-wise analyses localizing these effects mainly to dorsal SN-VTA regions. In contrast, LC CR was higher in URS than in FLR (d = 0.99), whereas URS did not differ significantly from HCs. NM-MRI signals were not associated with symptom severity or cognitive measures. These findings support the view that schizophrenia treatment-response subgroups may differ in long-term monoaminergic-related (NM-MRI) signal patterns. Elevated NM-MRI signal within dopaminergic nuclei may characterize both antipsychotic-responsive and clozapine nonresponsive schizophrenia, whereas additional noradrenergic involvement may contribute to severe treatment resistance. NM-MRI may help characterize biologically meaningful heterogeneity within treatment-resistant schizophrenia.

title: Altered effective connectivity during cognitive distancing in cognitive behavioral therapy nonresponders with depression.
abstract: Approximately half of individuals with major depressive disorder (MDD) do not respond to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Cognitive distancing is a reappraisal tactic central to CBT, and neural responses during reappraisal have been linked to psychotherapy outcome. We examined whether pretreatment effective connectivity during cognitive distancing was associated with CBT response in adults with MDD. Seventy-seven outpatients with MDD (31 women) completed fMRI during a distancing task before 25 CBT sessions as part of the SPeED trial, which included a pre-CBT phase of exercise or waiting list. Dynamic causal modeling estimated effective connectivity within a 10-region network. Group differences were assessed with parametric empirical Bayes, and predictive utility was evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation. Responders (n = 39) showed greater relative modulation along a dorsomedial-to-ventrolateral prefrontal-to-superior frontal/pre-supplementary motor area cascade during distancing, whereas nonresponders exhibited greater relative modulation of amygdala-to-ventrolateral prefrontal cortex connectivity. Nonresponders showed decreased dorsolateral prefrontal self-inhibition during negative picture processing, consistent with heightened local excitability. Distancing-related effects exceeded 99% posterior probability and predicted treatment response in cross-validation (r = .21-.31, p < .05). Effective connectivity during distancing robustly differentiated responders from nonresponders, with nonresponders showing weaker intra-prefrontal control and stronger amygdala-to-prefrontal influence. These neural patterns contribute to insight into CBT nonresponse and suggest a mechanism associated with lowered symptom improvement through cognitive interventions. However, incremental predictive value beyond baseline clinical measures was modest. If replicated prospectively, such measures may contribute to multimodal prediction models and adjunctive treatment strategies. Neurobiological correlates and mechanisms of the augmentation of psychotherapy with endurance exercise in mild to moderate depression - SPeED, http://apps.who.int/trialsearch/Trial2.aspx?TrialID=DRKS00008869, DRKS00008869.

title: Co-existent autoimmune diseases in people with multiple sclerosis and a review on choice of immunotherapy.
abstract: Coexisting autoimmune diseases in multiple sclerosis (MS) may influence disease-modifying therapy (DMT) choice, but Indian data remains limited. This study aims to determine the prevalence of co-existent autoimmune disorders in Indian MS patients and assess their impact on DMT selection. This multicentre, cross-sectional observational study included 355 adults with MS evaluated across five Indian neuroimmunology clinics between 2016 and 2026. Comorbidity prevalence was compared against general-population estimates, and DMT utilization was compared between patients with and without autoimmune comorbidities. Fifty-nine patients (16.6%) had an autoimmune disorder, with hypothyroidism (5.9%), rheumatoid arthritis (RA; 2.0%), and type 1 diabetes mellitus (1.4%) being the most common. Prevalences of RA (2.0% vs 0.49%; p = 0.002) and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD; 0.8% vs 0.02%; p < 0.001) were significantly higher than population estimates. Comorbidities shifted treatment: Rituximab use was lower in the comorbidity group (49.2% vs 69.3%; p = 0.003); dimethyl fumarate (22.0% vs 1.4%; p < 0.001) and azathioprine (5.1% vs 0.7%; p = 0.004) were prescribed more frequently. Autoimmune comorbidity occurred in about 1/6 Indian MS patients, with excess RA and IBD relative to population prevalence and an associated shift in DMT selection.

title: The blood-brain barrier and strategies for drug delivery to brain tumors.
abstract: Drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains an important challenge in the treatment of brain tumors. This review summarizes the physiologic barriers to effective CNS drug exposure and evaluates strategies to improve delivery, with a focus on glioma. Recent advances span three complementary approaches: engineering therapeutics for BBB penetration, transient BBB disruption, and locoregional delivery to bypass the BBB. Modern medicinal chemistry has enabled highly brain-penetrant agents such as vorasidenib, while transporter/receptor-mediated and nanocarrier platforms remain under investigation. Ultrasound with microbubbles has emerged as a leading strategy for spatially targeted, reversible BBB disruption, with early clinical studies demonstrating increased delivery of chemotherapies and monoclonal antibodies. Convection-enhanced delivery has benefited from improved catheter design, image guidance, and implantable systems, although efficacy in brain tumors remains unproven. Intratumoral oncolytic viruses and CSF-based cellular therapies are additional emerging approaches. Strategies for drug delivery to brain tumors have advanced substantially, but translation remains challenging. Efficacious therapies must not only overcome the BBB but also achieve adequate exposure and target engagement across heterogeneous tumor regions. Future studies must pair active therapeutics with relevant delivery strategies, ascertain drug exposure and target engagement early through window-of-opportunity studies, and evaluate efficacy in randomized trials.

title: Roadmap for cognitive neurorehabilitation: challenges and opportunities.
abstract: Cognitive deficits affect 40-50% of patients after acquired brain injury, with a profound impact on participation, work capacity and quality of life. Cognitive neurorehabilitation is a relevant and promising approach to promote cognitive recovery, but the evidence remains limited. This review discusses the clinical state-of-the-art, open questions in clinical research, and outlines a roadmap for future development of this rapidly evolving domain. While optimal contemporary cognitive neurorehabilitation is multimodal and interprofessional, the currently available evidence is diluted by heterogeneous treatment content and patient characteristics, as well as by inadequate methodology and reporting. Several questions remain open: the optimal dose and frequency of therapy, the preferable sequence of treatments, and the factors that moderate treatment effects. We highlight the pressing need for rigorously designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with active control conditions, everyday-relevant outcome measures, time by group interaction analyses and long-term follow-up. Future development of cognitive neurorehabilitation depends on RCTs and single-case experiments using cutting-edge methodology. We propose a roadmap with four tiers: mechanisms and efficacy, assessment of moderating factors, clinical validity as well as consideration of socio-economic impact and implementation from the outset. International collaboration in designing, developing and validating the approaches is warranted to ensure standardization and broad uptake. These efforts will promote the quality and accessibility of cognitive neurorehabilitation.

title: The cognitive and technological era in neurorehabilitation.
Handedness and race interact to shape support for Donald Trump: Evidence from three U.S. presidential election cycles.
journal: Politics and the life sciences : the journal of the Association for Politics and the Life Sciences
abstract: We examined neuro- and social-cognitive determinants of Trump support in a cross-sectional survey study encompassing the 2016, 2020, and 2024 elections. Using handedness as a window into neurofunction, we found that highly consistent use of one hand, versus relatively inconsistent handedness, was associated with multiple measures of Trump support. The direction of the association (positive or negative) depended on the social factor of race. We obtained multiple handedness X race interactions whereby consistently handed White individuals supported Trump more, but consistently handed non-White individuals supported him less. Regardless of race, consistent handedness was associated with greater authoritarian submission. These findings suggest a neurosociocognitive model of Trump support. Asymmetries of neurofunction, which co-occur with consistent handedness, predispose individuals to authoritarianism, and authoritarianism either increases or decreases Trump support depending on social (racial) identity. Neurobiology, cognition, and social factors may likewise influence Americans' response to authoritarian messaging in the post-Trump political environment.

title: Trainee psychiatrists' views on clozapine prescribing in Ireland.
abstract: Clozapine is the only licensed medication with established efficacy for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet it remains underutilised internationally. Delayed initiation is associated with poorer clinical outcomes, and clinician-related factors contribute to underuse. Limited research has examined trainee psychiatrists' knowledge and experience of clozapine prescribing. A cross-sectional online survey was distributed via the College of Psychiatrists of Ireland to approximately 500 psychiatry trainees between June 2024 and January 2025. The questionnaire assessed clinical experience, knowledge, confidence in clozapine management and perceived barriers to initiation. Seventy-four trainee psychiatrists completed the survey (response rate 14.8%). Most respondents had clinical exposure to clozapine; but fewer than one-third reported receiving specific clinical training. Knowledge regarding the indication for clozapine in TRS was strong, while knowledge relating to therapeutic drug monitoring, dosing and agranulocytosis risk was more variable. Respondents reported positive attitudes towards clozapine's effectiveness and safety. Confidence was highest in identifying TRS and monitoring mental health during treatment, but was lower for physical health monitoring, managing adverse-effects, discontinuation and rechallenge. Perceived barriers included concerns regarding adherence, blood monitoring requirements, adverse effects, and delays associated with hospital admission. Most respondents reported insufficient training in clozapine prescribing. Respondents reported positive perceptions of clozapine and good knowledge of its indication for TRS, although practical prescribing knowledge appeared more variable. Most reported limited formal training and low confidence in several practical aspects of clozapine management. Structured clozapine education and supervised clinical experience may improve trainee confidence and preparedness for clozapine prescribing.

title: Importance of recognising faciobrachial dystonic seizures in LGI1 antibody autoimmune encephalitis.
During natural vision, semantic novelty modulates fixation-related processing in primate cortex.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: We sample visual scenes with short gaze fixations separated by saccades. While low-level integration is known, semantic integration of foveal vision across fixations remains unclear. We hypothesized that the brain responds to changes in semantic information from one fixation to the next, and therefore postulated a neural signal associated with semantic novelty for each saccade. Novelty was measured from different layers of a deep network on foveal vision. Only semantic, and not low- or mid-level, novelty modulated frontal and occipital fixation-related potentials in male and female human scalp EEG during natural viewing of full-length movies (3.4x106 saccades). Intracranial recordings in male and female humans (9.0x104 saccades) and female non-human primates (Macaca mulatta; 3.3x104 saccades) revealed broadband high-frequency activity modulations in scene-specific ventral visual and frontal brain areas only for semantic novelty. This modulation was stronger for movies than static images, and frontal modulation occurred early alongside occipital modulation, suggesting top-down effects. This modulation of fixation-related activity with novelty suggests that foveal representations are compared between consecutive fixations to construct scene representations during natural viewing in primates.Significance statement Primate vision relies on eye movements to sample the world, yet how the brain integrates high-level meaning across these "snapshots" remains a mystery. By combining deep-learning models with massive electrophysiological datasets from humans and macaques, we show that the brain responds to changes in semantic content between fixations, but not low- or mid-level changes. We identified a "semantic novelty" signal that modulates neural activity across the primate cortex. These findings suggest visual processing is not a series of independent glimpses, but a continuous process comparing consecutive foveal information at the semantic level. This work bridges biological vision and artificial intelligence, providing a new framework for understanding how the brain maintains a coherent understanding of a dynamic world.

title: The nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract is required for learning odor-guided food avoidance.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Foraging animals must continually evaluate whether potential food sources are safe to consume. Such decisions rely on both innate preferences and learned associations formed through prior experience. Consumption of a food followed by malaise or sickness leads to avoidance of that food, reflecting learned associations between sensory cues that identify a food and its negative post-ingestive consequences. Although this form of learning has been studied extensively using taste cues, taste signals arise only after oral contact, at which point exposure to potential toxins has already occurred. Olfactory cues, in contrast, provide information about potential food sources prior to consumption, yet how odors acquire aversive value remains unclear. Here, using targeted chemogenetic perturbations, we identify the nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract (NLOT), which has direct bidirectional connectivity to olfactory regions and the basolateral amygdala, as a critical circuit element for odor-aversion learning in male and female mice. We find that the NLOT is required for conditioned odor aversion but is dispensable for other odor-guided behaviors and for fear conditioning driven by a non-olfactory cue. Our findings identify a selective role for the NLOT in linking olfactory cues to learned aversive outcomes, that supports odor-guided behavioral decisions.Significance statement Animals rely on smell to evaluate food safety before consuming it, yet the brain circuits that link odor cues to learned aversive outcomes remain poorly understood. Here we identify the nucleus of the lateral olfactory tract (NLOT), a largely unstudied region at the interface between olfactory and limbic circuits, as a critical and selective node for conditioned odor aversion learning. Chemogenetic perturbations of the NLOT disrupted both the acquisition and expression of odor-malaise associations, while leaving odor detection, odor discrimination, and non-olfactory fear learning intact - revealing a previously unrecognized specialization within olfactory-amygdala circuits that supports odor-guided decisions about food safety.

title: Subliminal beauty engages the brain's valuation circuits.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Neuroeconomic models propose that the anterior ventral striatum (aVS) and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) are key regions for computing subjective value (SV) signals that guide choice. However, the role of conscious awareness in this process remains debated. Here we examined whether SV can be automatically computed in these regions without conscious awareness. In an fMRI experiment, human participants (24 females, 5 males) viewed faces that varied in attractiveness under three conditions: (i) suppressed from awareness via continuous flash suppression (CFS), (ii) clearly visible without suppression, or (iii) absent (background only) with CFS. Participants reported trial-wise facial identity (objective) and visibility (subjective) measures of facial awareness. In a post-fMRI session, they rated the attractiveness of each face as a measure of SV. When faces were seen, task performance (d') exceeded chance and responses were faster than in absent trials. When faces were unseen, performance was at chance but responses were slower than absent trials. Neurally, seen and unseen faces elicited greater neural signal than absent trials and showed similar neural patterns in the fusiform face area (FFA). Critically, neural signal in vmPFC correlated with SV for both seen and unseen faces, with similar neural patterns. In aVS, SV-related signal was only observed for unseen faces. Furthermore, mean face-related signal in FFA correlated with SV-related signals in aVS and vmPFC for unseen faces. These findings demonstrate that SV can be automatically computed in aVS and vmPFC without conscious awareness, suggesting a neural pathway by which subliminal information can influence value-based choice.Significance statement A central question in consciousness research and decision neuroscience is whether the brain's valuation circuitry - particularly the anterior ventral striatum (aVS) and ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) - can compute subjective value automatically without conscious awareness. This question is important because prevailing accounts often assume that cognitive functions supported by the prefrontal cortex require conscious awareness of task-relevant information. Using continuous flash suppression and neuroimaging, we found that faces reported unseen nevertheless evoked value-related signals in aVS and vmPFC that scaled with subjective attractiveness ratings. These findings demonstrate that subjective value can be computed automatically from social information in the absence of conscious awareness.

title: Multi-Site Quality Assurance of ADC and PDFF Measurements: A Multi-Vendor Phantom Study.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
abstract: Reliable quantitative imaging biomarkers are important for multi-site studies. However, scanner- and site-specific variations can compromise the clinical utility of many measures including apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) and proton density fat fraction (PDFF). Phantom-based quality assurance provides a foundation for multi-site studies. To evaluate cross-site reproducibility, intra-session reliability, and accuracy of ADC and PDFF measurements across four sites. Prospective phantom study. A NIST diffusion phantom (CaliberMRI, Model 128) and a fat phantom (Calimetrix, Model 300). 3 T/diffusion-weighted spin-echo echo-planar imaging for ADC and 3D gradient-echo imaging for PDFF. ADC and PDFF were measured to assess cross-site reproducibility and intra-session reliability. Accuracy was evaluated against reference values. Intra-session repeatability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Intra-session measurement variability was quantified using the coefficient of variation (CoV), and agreement between repeated measurements was assessed using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (LCCC). NRMSE (normalized root mean square error) assessed accuracy relative to reference values. A linear mixed-effects (LME) model assessed site differences in ADC and PDFF, with p 0.99). Mean NRMSE between measured and reference values was < 10.0% for ADC and < 7.0% for PDFF, suggesting high accuracy. Mean intra-session CoV was < 1.0% for ADC and < 2.0% for PDFF, while LCCC exceeded 0.99 for both measurements, demonstrating strong agreement. LME models showed significant site effects for both ADC (F(3, 36) = 6.05) and PDFF (F(3, 33) = 5.07), while pairwise differences met the prespecified equivalence criteria for both measures. Diffusion and fat phantoms provide reliable quality assurance tools for quantitative ADC and PDFF measurements across multiple MRI sites, supporting consistency despite statistically significant site effects. 4. Stage 1.

title: Redox-encoded molecular recognition enables enzyme-free potentiometric sensing of electroinactive glutamate.
abstract: Glutamate (Glu), the major excitatory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system, is intrinsically electroinactive, making its direct electrochemical detection challenging and often requiring enzyme-mediated signal transduction. Here, we introduce a redox-encoded molecular recognition strategy that converts selective binding of electroinactive Glu into a potentiometric signal without enzymatic catalysis. The resulting glutamate potentiometric redox-encoded sensor (Glu-PRES) integrates a molecularly imprinted polydopamine (PDA) recognition layer with a Prussian Blue (PB) redox transducer on a bipolar carbon fiber electrode. Selective Glu binding within the imprinted cavities modulates the local interfacial environment and ionic accessibility of the underlying PB layer, inducing a PB-associated potential shift that is measured against a stable IrCl63-/IrCl62- redox interface through galvanic potentiometry. Glu-PRES provides a broad linear range of 0.10-400 μM with a detection limit of 31 nM, while responses to physiologically relevant interferents remain below 14% of that to 10 μM Glu. The sensor also exhibits reversible potential responses upon repeated switching between 100 nM and 1 μM Glu, together with strong resistance to protein fouling. The sensor further resolves graded Glu-release dynamics in a brain hematoma-mimicking hydrogel model. These results demonstrate a recognition-to-redox potential encoding strategy for enzyme-free potentiometric sensing of electroinactive molecular targets.

title: Is metformin use associated with cognitive, physical and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults with type 2 diabetes? A secondary analysis of the SCOPE multicentre prospective cohort study.
Longitudinal Associations of Changes in Body Mass Index and Waist-to-Height Ratio With Cardiometabolic Risk Factors: Sex-Specific Analyses in UK Biobank.
abstract: To examine associations of within-person changes in body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) with cardiometabolic outcomes, characterise dose-response non-linearity and investigate effect modification by sex. In this observational UK Biobank cohort, participants had repeated anthropometric and biochemical measurements approximately 4 years apart. Those with baseline cardiovascular disease, renal failure or cancer were excluded. Associations of BMI and WHtR change with cardiometabolic outcomes were examined using multivariable analysis of covariance and restricted cubic splines, with multiple imputation for missing data. Among 16 911 participants with a mean baseline BMI 26.8 kg/m2 (SD: 4.5), 679 experienced ≥ 10% BMI loss and 705 ≥ 10% gain over median 4.4 years. Compared with stable BMI (±5%), ≥ 10% loss was associated with lower systolic blood pressure (-6.11 mmHg; 95% CI: -7.14 to -5.07), triglycerides (-23.4%; -25.7 to -21.0) and C-reactive protein (-39.5%; -43.7 to -35.1), with lower DBP, total and LDL cholesterol, HbA1c and SCORE2 and higher HDL cholesterol. Conversely, ≥ 10% gain was associated with higher SBP (+4.23 mmHg; 3.22-5.23), triglycerides (+16.9%; 13.4-20.5) and C-reactive protein (+45.7%; 36.0-56.1), with adverse differences across most outcomes. Associations were broadly similar for BMI and WHtR, with non-linearity for selected outcomes. Sex modified associations with DBP, lipids and SCORE2, with larger triglyceride reductions accompanying BMI loss in men. Adiposity reduction was associated with favourable cardiometabolic profiles, whereas gain was associated with adverse profiles. BMI and WHtR showed broadly similar directions and patterns of association, with some variation by outcome and sex. These observational associations support prevention of excess adiposity gain and sustained adiposity reduction where clinically appropriate.

title: Suspected SCALP syndrome (sebaceous nevus, CNS malformations, aplasia cutis congenita, limbal dermoid, and pigmented nevus) and the spectrum of mosaic RASopathies: ophthalmic and systemic manifestations in a paediatric cohort.
abstract: To describe the clinical spectrum of the ophthalmic and systemic manifestations in children suspected as having SCALP (Sebaceous Nevus, CNS Malformations, Aplasia Cutis Congenita, Limbal Dermoid, and Pigmented Nevus) syndrome. We reviewed the medical records of 13 children suspected to have SCALP syndrome between 1 January 2016 and 31 March 2025. Their demographic details and clinical findings were analyzed. Median age at presentation was 1.2 years (range: 5 days to 10 years). Of the 13 patients, 6 (46.2%) were aged ≤ 1 year. The cohort comprised 9 males and 4 females. One patient was born to consanguineous parents. Ocular involvement was bilateral in 6 patients and unilateral in 7. Among the cohort, two children had the complete SCALP phenotype, three presented with partial features, and eight had features of probable mosaic RASopathy. The most consistent clinical findings were limbal dermoids, which were present in all cases except one. Twelve children had scalp findings, with four having aplasia cutis and eight having nevus psiloliparus. Additional ocular features included dermolipomas, upper eyelid coloboma, ptosis, and limbal stem cell deficiency. Systemic manifestations observed included sebaceous nevi, developmental delay, epilepsy with cortical dysplasia. SCALP syndrome is a rare neurocutaneous disorder with consistent oculocutaneous features and variable neurological involvement. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are essential. Developing structured diagnostic criteria and exploring genotypic-phenotypic links would be critical to improving outcomes. SCALP syndrome is best regarded as lying within the spectrum of mosaic RASopathies; in the absence of lesional molecular testing, the diagnosis in individual cases should be considered provisional, with aplasia cutis congenita serving as the key clinical discriminator.

title: Ketamine for Co-occurring Chronic Pain and Depression: A Scoping Review fing the Dual-Outcome Evidence Gap and Its Treatment and Research Implications.
abstract: Chronic pain and depression frequently co-occur, share clinical features, and involve shared neurobiological substrates. Ketamine, an NMDA-receptor antagonist, has established antidepressant efficacy, whereas its analgesic efficacy for chronic pain remains uncertain. Given the overlap between chronic pain and depression, ketamine may serve as a potential dual-action treatment. We conducted a scoping review of studies in which pain and depressive outcomes were both assessed longitudinally after ketamine treatment. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus through August 2026. Experimental and observational studies reporting post-treatment pain and depression outcomes were included; acute, perioperative, perinatal, and cancer-related pain were excluded. Of 2,187 records screened, 12 studies met inclusion criteria (2007-2025). Eight enrolled patients with consensus-based chronic pain (≥3 months); among these, only two used clinical diagnoses to characterize depression (one being retrospective chart review), whereas the remainder used symptom scales. Four depression-primary studies enrolled patients with major depressive disorder, treatment-resistant depression, or bipolar depression but did not rigorously establish chronic pain duration. Most studies reported concurrent improvement in pain and depressive symptoms, but heterogeneity in population definitions, ketamine administration regimens, study design, and psychiatric comorbidity precludes inference that depression modifies ketamine's analgesic effect. Prospective randomized studies using standardized chronic pain and depression measures are needed to clarify ketamine's efficacy and real-world applicability. REGISTRATION: This protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (OSF) (registration: OSF.IO/3ER5W) PERSPECTIVE: This review maps studies that assessed pain and depressive symptoms longitudinally during ketamine treatment. Concurrent improvement was commonly reported, but inconsistent depression ascertainment, pain phenotyping, dosing, and study design prevent conclusions about depression-specific analgesic effects. Prospective trials with clinically defined comorbidity are needed.

title: Day-to-day migraine-related disability and mental health in children and adolescents with migraine: a longitudinal prospective cohort study.
abstract: Migraine affects 11% of youth and causes substantial functional impairment. While youth with migraine exhibit elevated pain catastrophizing and internalizing symptoms, daily associations with migraine-related disability remain unclear due to limited longitudinal research. This study examined associations between migraine-related disability on headache days (1) state pain catastrophizing, same-day mood, and anxiety, and (2) mood and anxiety 24-48 hours before and after a reported headache day. In a 30-day prospective cohort from a tertiary pediatric headache program, 53 participants (8-18 years; median age 15; 87% female; 57% chronic migraine) reported 769 headache days via electronic diaries. Measures included a daily Pediatric Migraine Disability Assessment Scale (PedMIDAS), the 3-item State Pain Catastrophizing Scale for Children (SPCS-C), and 11-point numerical rating scales for mood/anxiety. Generalized negative binomial mixed-effects models were conducted. On headache days, higher state pain catastrophizing (IRR=1.03, 95% CI=1.01-1.05) and lower mood (IRR=0.92, 95% CI=0.87-0.97) significantly associated with greater disability. Higher anxiety was associated with greater disability in primary analyses, but this association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Mood and anxiety 24-48 hours before a headache day did not predict disability, nor did disability predict mood or anxiety 24-48 hours post-headache day. These findings suggest that same-day state pain catastrophizing and poor mood are associated with headache-day disability in youth, whereas short-term fluctuations in mood and anxiety surrounding a reported headache day are not. This suggests that psychological factors have an immediate, state-dependent association with functional impairment, highlighting the importance of "in-the-moment" psychological targets for clinical intervention. PERSPECTIVE: This study shows that same-day pain catastrophizing, mood, and anxiety are closely linked to migraine-related disability in youth, whereas short-term fluctuations surrounding headache days are not. Findings highlight immediate, state-dependent psychological mechanisms underlying functional impairment, suggesting targeted "in-the-moment" interventions may reduce disability and improve daily functioning in pediatric migraine.

title: Oxaliplatin induces spontaneous firing at sensory endings across touch and proprioceptive afferents.
abstract: Spontaneous activity in primary sensory neurons has been implicated in neuropathic symptoms, yet its earliest origins and immediate functional consequences remain incompletely understood. This gap is especially consequential in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), where sensory toxicities commonly limit effective cancer treatment. Using in vivo recordings in female rats, we show that a single high-dose of oxaliplatin (OX) induces spontaneous firing within 24 h across touch and proprioceptive low-threshold mechanoreceptor (LTMR) afferents. Spontaneous firing consistently originated distally in peripheral axons and was accompanied by enhanced responses to mechanical stimulation, identifying LTMR sensory endings as the earliest source of spontaneous firing and a common site for spontaneous and stimulus-evoked hyperexcitability. OX also induced early structural abnormalities at sensory endings; however, SF+ LTMRs retained mechanosensory response profiles, indicating that spontaneous firing can emerge within otherwise functional sensory endings. Although coincident spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity distorted encoding in individual LTMRs, its effects were attenuated in population-averaged responses and were not accompanied by detectable impairment of ladder-rung performance. Together, these findings identify sensory endings as an early target of OX neurotoxicity and demonstrate that spontaneous firing spanning multiple tactile and proprioceptive LTMR submodalities can coexist with stable performance on a proprioceptive-guided locomotor task. Abnormal activity initiated at sensory endings may therefore contribute to acute paraesthetic symptoms without measurably impairing the sensorimotor behavior examined here, whereas progression to chronic neuropathic symptoms may require subsequent recruitment of the dorsal root ganglion.

title: Smoking-Related Oral Health and Dental Aesthetic Signature: Digital and Clinical Findings from the SMILE Study.
abstract: To compare oral health, dental aesthetic, and patient-reported outcomes between current and never smokers in the SMILE cohort and characterize the oral signature associated with smoking. This analysis included 374 participants (308 current smokers, 66 never smokers). Gingival inflammation was assessed using the Modified Gingival Index (MGI), extrinsic staining using the MacPherson-modified Lobene Stain Index (MLSI), tooth colour using the Whiteness Index for Dentistry (WID), and plaque/tartar using quantitative light-induced fluorescence (ΔR30, ΔR120) and the Simple Oral Hygiene (SOH) score. Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) and self-perceived general health (EQ-VAS) were also assessed. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, and nationality. In the unadjusted analysis, never smokers showed lower MGI (p < 0.0001), buccal (p = 0.002) and lingual MLSI (p < 0.0001), ΔR30 (p = 0.013), ΔR120 (p = 0.004) and SOH (p = 0.001), and higher WID (p = 0.004) and EQ-VAS (p < 0.0001) than smokers, whereas OHRQoL did not differ (p = 0.137). After adjustment, never-smoking status remained associated with lower MGI, staining, and SOH and higher WID and EQ-VAS. Associations with ΔR30 and ΔR120 were attenuated and no longer significant. Current smoking was independently associated with an oral signature characterized by greater gingival inflammation and extrinsic staining, reduced tooth whiteness, poorer oral hygiene, and lower perceived general health. Combining calibrated digital measures with established clinical indices provides a reproducible approach to characterizing smoking-related oral differences and monitoring changes following smoking cessation or substitution. ClinicalTrials.gov ID, NCT04649645, Date registration: Nov 25, 2020.

title: Single Neonatal Maternal Separation Alters Ultrasonic Vocalization during Mother-Offspring Interaction in ICR Mice.
abstract: Early-life stress is a major risk factor for neurodevelopmental disorders; however, the extent to which temporally restricted stress exposure induces long-term behavioral alterations remains unclear. In this study, we examined the effects of a single 24-h maternal separation (MS) during postnatal days 4-5 (P4-5) on later behavior in mice. MS males showed mildly reduced locomotor activity, whereas no statistically significant Control-MS differences were detected in the measured indices of anxiety-like behavior or sociability. In the novel object recognition test, neither group showed a significant preference for the novel object, limiting conclusions regarding recognition memory. We further examined ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) across development and social contexts. Under isolated conditions, USV call number did not significantly differ between Control and MS mice, although MS mice showed longer USV duration at P14. More USV calls were recorded from MS male-biological mother pairs than from Control male-biological mother pairs at P42, whereas no statistically significant Control-MS differences were detected during interactions with an unfamiliar mother or a virgin female during P41-P43. A significant Sex × Treatment interaction was detected in the biological-mother condition, although the interaction across social-partner conditions did not reach statistical significance. In a separate sound-source localization experiment, offspring were the predominant identified USV emitters during mother-offspring interactions in both Control and MS dyads, although offspring-assigned USV call numbers did not differ significantly between Control and MS groups under these recording conditions. Together, these findings indicate that a single neonatal MS experience is associated with later alterations in social vocalization, with increased USV emission detected during interactions between P42 MS males and their biological mothers. The mechanisms underlying this response, including the possible contributions of familiarity, prior maternal experience, and other maternal cues, remain to be determined.

title: Allopregnanolone enantiomers prevent acute adverse effects of erastin-induced stress on hippocampal plasticity & learning.
abstract: Neuroactive steroids (NAS), including allopregnanolone (AlloP), have emerged as treatments for neuropsychiatric illnesses. Therapeutic NAS are positive allosteric modulators of GABAA receptors but also have important alternative targets beyond GABA. Here we found that brief administration of erastin, an agent that promotes cellular stress via System Xc- exchangers and voltage-dependent anion channels (VDACs), had no effect on basal transmission in the Schaffer collateral pathway of rat hippocampal slices, but acutely inhibited long-term potentiation (LTP). LTP effects were prevented by VBIT-4, an inhibitor of VDAC oligomerization, and by inhibitors of the NLRP3 inflammasome and caspase-1. Effects of erastin on LTP were also prevented by AlloP and, at lower concentrations, its unnatural enantiomer (ent-AlloP), a steroid that unlike AlloP has weak effects on GABAA receptors. Protective effects of AlloP enantiomers were prevented by inhibition of liver X receptors (LXRs) that mediate certain intracellular effects of NAS. Erastin also dampened learning in a hippocampal-dependent form of one-trial memory; these effects were prevented by VBIT-4, an LXR agonist and ent-AlloP, but not by a non-sedating dose of AlloP. These results have relevance for understanding NAS as modulators of neuronal stress and for further development of NAS therapeutics.

title: Beyond neurones: cardiac involvement in motor neurone disease.
abstract: Motor neurone disease (MND) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder defined by the progressive loss of upper and lower motor neurones. This degeneration leads to muscle wasting and weakness, most prominently affecting the upper and lower limbs, the bulbar musculature responsible for speech and swallowing, as well as the respiratory muscles (Feldman et al., 2022). As the disease advances, affected individuals experience profound functional decline, loss of independence, and ultimately respiratory failure, which remains the leading cause of death (Kiernan et al., 2021). Despite advances in understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms of MND, effective disease‑modifying treatments are limited and there is no cure. Management therefore focuses largely on symptomatic treatment and multidisciplinary supportive care to maintain quality of life (Simon et al., 2015). The long-standing view of MND as a disease confined to the motor system is increasingly being challenged. Emerging evidence from human and rodent studies suggests that other organ systems, such as the heart, may also be affected, raising the possibility that cardiac involvement is a clinically relevant but under‑recognised feature of the disease.

title: Regional cortical thinning in cerebral small vessel disease: associations with disease burden and cognitive and motor impairment.
abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a major cause of cognitive decline and mobility impairment, yet whether cortical thickness and cortical volume provide similar or complementary information across different levels of CSVD burden remains unclear. We examined regional cortical thickness and cortical volume in healthy controls and participants with CSVD using high-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging and FreeSurfer-based parcellation. Greater CSVD burden was associated with thinning across bilateral insular, occipital, temporal, cingulate, and cuneal regions, whereas cortical volume alterations were more spatially restricted, with only the left parahippocampal gyrus surviving Bonferroni correction. After adjustment for demographic characteristics, vascular risk factors, apolipoprotein E genotype, and mean cortical thickness, associations remained evident in the bilateral insulae and selected occipital and temporal regions. Regional cortical thickness was also related to cognitive and mobility performance. Exploratory incremental analyses showed that regional cortical thickness remained associated with cognitive performance in several regions after accounting for the corresponding regional cortical volume, intracranial volume, and other covariates. These findings suggest that cortical thickness and cortical volume may capture partly distinct aspects of cortical morphology in CSVD, with cortical thickness potentially providing complementary information related to cognitive performance.

title: Structural changes in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex following a randomized clinical trial of virtual reality-based cognitive remediation in mood and schizophrenia spectrum disorders.
abstract: Cognitive impairments are common in patients with mood disorders (MD) and schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD) and impair quality of life. Developing pro-cognitive treatments is hindered by limited understanding of the biology underlying cognitive impairment and improvement. This structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) study examined the neural correlates of cognitive improvement following a Virtual-Reality-based Cognitive Remediation Therapy (VR-CRT) intervention. Patients underwent eight VR-CRT or VR-control treatment sessions during a four-week period. The study population included data from a transdiagnostic subsample of 41 symptomatically stable, cognitively impaired patients with MD or SSD (VR-CRT: n = 22; VR-control: n = 19) with baseline structural MRI data of which 33 (VR-CRT: 20; VR-control: n = 13) also underwent MRI at treatment completion. Neuropsychological assessment was completed both pre- and post-treatment and additionally at three-month post-treatment follow-up. Gray matter volume in the VR-CRT group increased over time in the right caudal middle frontal gyrus (MFG) compared to VR-control. Secondary hypothesis-driven analysis showed a similar increase in right caudal MFG thickness for VR-CRT patients. These structural changes were not associated with treatment-related cognitive improvement. However, greater left rostral MFG thickness at baseline was associated with more cognitive improvement over time in the VR-CRT group. This study demonstrates treatment-related structural changes in the right caudal MFG and suggests that baseline left rostral MFG thickness may represent a candidate marker of cognitive improvement within the VR-CRT group. These findings support further investigation of MFG structure as a marker of brain response and cognitive treatment outcome. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06038955, and is completed.

title: Long lasting alterations of feeding by Adolescent obesity.
abstract: The prevalence of obesity is increasing worldwide, especially amongst younger populations. As both brain and body are still under development, numerous studies have shown that adolescence is an especially sensitive period for the impact of external insults including unbalanced diets. To better understand and prevent the vulnerability to obesity and maladaptive food choice, it is crucial to explore the long-term impact of adolescent exposure to obesogenic diets on different feeding behaviours. To address this, we gave mice access to an obesogenic diet with a very high-fat content (vHFD) specifically during adolescence and investigated the long-lasting impact on feeding at adulthood months after a switch to a healthy diet. Using specific feeding tests, we found that both males and females vHFD-exposed mice exhibited an increased intake of both standard food and palatable high-fat foods, without impacting preference for non-caloric food rewards. Importantly, these alterations are not fully correlated with diet-induced weight gain. The study reveals that the chronic consumption of energy-rich obesogenic diets during adolescence leads to long-lasting dysregulation of feeding, which may support long-term vulnerability to overeating and obesity.

title: Bioremediation of Chlorpyrifos Contaminated Soil: Microcosm Investigation and 16S rRNA Gene Amplicon Sequencing.
abstract: This study describes the isolation and characterization of two biofilm-forming bacterial strains, Pseudomonas aeruginosa MD3 and Bacillus toyonensis LD07, capable of degrading chlorpyrifos. These isolates demonstrated remarkable phenotypic plasticity, maintaining biofilm formation across varying pH, temperature and salinity levels. To maximize microbial stability and metabolic efficiency, sugarcane bagasse was utilized as a support matrix. Analytical characterization (EDX, BET and XRD) confirmed that the bagasse possesses a highly porous architecture, serving as a protective scaffold and an auxiliary carbon source for synergistic co-metabolism. A bio-product formulated via solid-state fermentation on this matrix exhibited exceptional bioremediation efficacy, eliminating 99% of chlorpyrifos at an extreme concentration of 4500 ppm within 35 days. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing of coffee-growing soils across different treatments (natural control, pesticide-stressed and 10% bio-product amended) with accession numbers PRJNA1529359 revealed distinct shifts in microbial community dynamics. While the taxonomic landscape was broadly dominated by Bacillota, Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota, the bio-product amendment caused P. aeruginosa and B. toyonensis to become the dominant taxa. Ultimately, these insights underscore the viability of cost-effective agricultural by-products for cell immobilization and highlight metagenomics as a powerful predictive framework for monitoring the remediation of anthropogenically stressed ecosystems.

title: An astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 axis promotes synapse engulfment in early amyloid pathology.
abstract: Region-specific synapse loss is an early hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, yet the upstream signals that render synapses vulnerable remain unclear. In a mouse model of amyloidosis, we identify an early astrocyte state that emerges in vulnerable brain regions before widespread plaque deposition and overt gliosis. These astrocytes exhibit bulbous-looking perisynaptic processes enriched in p62 and glycogen, impaired autophagic flux and calcium signaling, and diminished astrocyte-synapse coverage. Rather than exhibiting increased synapse engulfment, bulbous astrocytes show elevated milk fat globule-epidermal growth factor 8 (MFG-E8) and are associated with increased local microglial synapse engulfment. Astrocyte-specific gain- and loss-of-function experiments demonstrate that astrocyte-derived MFG-E8 is required for microglial synapse engulfment and acts through microglial β3 integrin signaling. Astrocytic Mfge8 deletion reduces microglial engulfment and synapse loss across amyloidosis models and is associated with reduced amyloid pathology, gliosis, and cognitive impairment. Together, these findings define an astrocyte-microglia MFG-E8 signaling axis that contributes to region-specific synaptic vulnerability during early amyloid pathology.

title: The representation of object-concept primitives across the macaque brain.
abstract: Object concepts are mental representations that provide information beyond immediate sensory input, but where and how the brain encodes them remains unresolved. Here, macaques spent years learning a set of object-concept primitives: two-dimensional stimuli, each defined by a paired association between a unique color and a unique shape. During fMRI, the animals were cued with one feature (shapeless color or colorless shape) and rewarded for subsequently identifying the associated feature. Using a new whole-brain searchlight inspired by convolutional networks, we identified regions that carried information about the unshown feature during cue presentation. Cross-feature decoding was absent in retinotopic cortex but present bilaterally in discrete foci in anterior inferior temporal cortex (aIT), the temporal pole (TP), and frontal cortex (FC). In aIT and TP, the geometry of the neural representation of shapes matched the color-circle geometry of the associated colors, whereas FC supported the best decoding of error trials. Additional passive-viewing experiments showed univariate fMRI response biases to the learned associations in extrastriate visual cortex, which may reflect feedback from regions identified by cross-feature decoding. Together, the results provide a blueprint for how the brain encodes object concepts and suggest how concept representations engage perceptual representations through feedback during vision.

title: Quantification of the flexural rigidity of endovascular surgical devices using three-point bending tests.
journal: Journal of the mechanical behavior of biomedical materials
abstract: Endovascular surgical procedures require the navigation of catheters and wires through the vasculature to reach distal target sites. Quantitative frameworks for device selection have the potential to improve navigation success by optimizing device flexural rigidity for a given patient-specific anatomy. However, data are lacking to facilitate this technology, in part because typical endovascular devices have intricate spatial variations in mechanical properties that are challenging and tedious to quantify repeatably. We therefore developed a three-point bend test methodology using a custom rig and applied it to measure lengthwise flexural rigidity profiles of devices commonly used in neuroendovascular procedures. The methodology demonstrated high repeatability and was able to characterize transition zones in detail. We applied the methodology to generate the first comprehensive, quantitative library of device flexural rigidities, spanning guidewires, intermediate guides, and long sheaths. We observed that these three classes of device have properties that fall into distinct ranges. Additional plots examining relationships between flexural rigidity, device diameter, and length revealed application-specific trends in flexural properties. This methodology and resulting data allow for standardized characterization and comparisons to aid device selection, and have the potential to both enhance surgical planning and inform future endovascular innovation.

title: Association of menopausal symptom burden with performance and self-monitoring across cognitive domains.
abstract: Perimenopause is a dynamic neuroendocrine transition with increased risk of cognitive, psychological and physical symptoms. How population variability in symptom burden relates to different aspects of cognitive functioning remains unclear. We measured menopausal symptom burden, task-specific cognitive performance, task confidence and metacognitive bias using the online platform "Cognitron" with 1614 participants aged 45-60 from the Great British Intelligence Test. Symptom burden was standardised (mean = 0, SD = 1), allowing coefficients to be interpreted in standard deviation (SD) units. Exploratory analyses showed early and late perimenopause to be a significant predictor of higher menopausal symptom burden (respectively 0.259 SD, 95% CI 0.116, 0.401, and 0.284 SD, CI 95% 0.115, 0.452, both p < 0.001). Global cognitive performance was significantly lower in individuals with higher symptom burden (-0.092 SD, 95% CI -0.133, -0.050, pFDR < 0.001, ηₚ2 = 0.0117). Higher symptom burden also predicted lower task confidence (-0.225 SD, 95% CI -0.272, -0.178, pFDR < 0.001, ηₚ2 = 0.0527) and negative bias (-0.135 SD, 95% CI -0.181, -0.089, pFDR < 0.001, ηₚ2 = 0.0206). Exploratory analyses showed that symptom burden significantly predicted poorer performance on tasks measuring executive function (Stroop interference), working memory (digit span), spatial reasoning (block design), and verbal analogical reasoning. Our findings highlight menopausal symptom burden as a significant predictor of cognitive and metacognitive differences and longitudinal research is needed to identify those at greatest risk of cognitive decline.

title: Is the number of strength and hop tests passed at the time of return to pre-injury sport level associated with second ACL injury? A registry study of 458 patients.
journal: Physical therapy in sport : official journal of the Association of Chartered Physiotherapists in Sports Medicine
abstract: To analyze whether the number of strength and hop tests passed in a 5-test battery was associated with the hazard of second ACL injury after returning to pre-injury level of sports (RTS). Registry-based cohort study. Data extracted in February 2026 from a rehabilitation registry. Patients aged 15-35 years at the time of primary ACL reconstruction with ipsilateral hamstring or patellar tendon autograft and pre-injury Tegner activity level ≥ 6. Second ACL injury after RTS, assessed during available follow-up and within one year of RTS using a Cox proportional hazard regression model. Hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated and p-value was set to < 0.05. 458 patients were included. 60 (13%) second ACL injuries occurred within all available follow-up time, where 32 (7.0%) occurred within 1 year after RTS. No significant association was observed between number of tests passed and second ACL injury during available follow-up (p = 0.41), or within one year of RTS (p = 0.87), after adjustment for autograft type, time to RTS, and BMI. The number of tests passed in a 5-test muscle function battery was not associated with the hazard of second ACL injury after RTS.

title: Integrated multi-omics identifies PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte state remodeling in paraquat-associated Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is an environmentally relevant herbicide associated with neurotoxicity and Parkinson's disease (PD) risk, yet the key molecular determinants linking PQ exposure to PD and the cellular states in which these alterations occur remain incompletely understood. We integrated network toxicology, human PD transcriptomics, machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, spatial metabolomics, virtual perturbation, model-inferred protein analysis, molecular docking, and tissue validation to characterize PQ-associated molecular and cellular remodeling. Integrating PQ-associated targets with PD-related genes identified 293 candidates, among which prostaglandin D2 synthase (PTGDS) was consistently prioritized by random forest, XGBoost, and LASSO, with its PD-associated expression pattern reproduced across the discovery and independent validation cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized Ptgds expression predominantly to oligodendrocytes and identified two PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte (MOL) states with PQ-associated compositional patterns. CytoTRACE placed these PTGDS-enriched populations among relatively mature oligodendrocyte states. Functional analyses revealed distinct state-specific programs, with Ptgds+Mag+ MOL associated with myelin-associated programs, axon ensheathment-related programs, cholesterol metabolism, and lipid transport, whereas Ptgds+Il33+ MOL was linked to neuron-interaction-related programs, synaptic organization, cell adhesion, and neuron-glia communication. Ligand-receptor inference and spatial analyses supported state-specific changes in neuron-glia communication and spatial relationships. Spatial metabolomics showed significantly increased phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin signals in regions with higher inferred representation of Ptgds+Mag+ MOL states. Virtual Ptgds perturbation and scTranslator-based protein prediction further suggested state-specific myelin-lipid and neuron-interaction programs, while molecular docking provided preliminary structural predictions regarding a potential PQ-PTGDS interaction. Immunofluorescence further confirmed PTGDS localization in mature oligodendrocytes within the substantia nigra. Collectively, these findings identify PTGDS-enriched mature oligodendrocyte states as cellular contexts associated with PQ-related brain remodeling and extend our understanding of PQ neurotoxicity beyond classical neuron-centered mechanisms. This integrative framework provides mechanistic insight into how an environmental neurotoxicant may reshape myelin-lipid homeostasis and neuron-glia interactions in the context of PD-related brain pathology.

title: Salidroside regulates blood-brain barrier integrity via Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis inhibition for high-altitude hypoxic brain injury intervention.
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
abstract: High-altitude hypoxic brain injury (HHBI) is a central nervous system injury disease induced by high-altitude hypobaric and hypoxic environment, which disrupts normal cerebral metabolism and neurological function and triggers multi-dimensional pathological damage in brain tissues. Among these pathological events, blood-brain barrier (BBB) injury represents a critical initiating and aggravating facet of HHBI, which drives subsequent cerebral inflammation, cerebral edema and progressive brain tissue deterioration. Current clinically commonly used drugs can only relieve partial discomforts caused by high-altitude hypoxia, and fail to achieve precise prevention and treatment of HHBI as well as favorable safety profile prognosis. Salidroside (Sal), the core active ingredient of the classic Tibetan medicine Rhodiola crenulata, exerts prominent anti-hypoxia and neuroprotective effects, yet its specific molecular regulatory mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. Combining in vivo and in vitro experiments, this study aimed to explore the novel mechanism by which Sal alleviates BBB injury and thereby prevents and treats HHBI via regulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. After acclimatization, mice were randomly assigned to control, model, dexamethasone (0.5 mg/kg), and Sal (50 and 100 mg/kg) groups, followed by 7-day consecutive administration of corresponding drugs. A low-pressure oxygen chamber was used to simulate high-altitude environments to establish the mouse HHBI model. The WBP respiratory detection system and Morris water maze test were employed to assess alterations in respiratory function and memory cognitive capacity of HHBI mice. A hematology analyzer and H&E staining were utilized to characterize systemic and cerebral inflammatory injury, whereas evans blue staining and brain water content measurement were performed to evaluate hypoxic impacts on BBB permeability. Super-resolution imaging (NIR-Ⅱ imaging and TEM) was adopted to detect cerebral microvascular blood circulation and ultrastructural alterations. Subsequently, RNA-seq was conducted to screen potential molecular targets mediating Sal conferred therapeutic effects against HHBI. Moreover, molecular docking, DFT calculation, alanine scanning and LSPR analysis were implemented to simulate the binding potential and stability between Sal and proteins of the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis, and protein-protein docking and Co-IP further verified the potential binding and regulatory interaction between Lcn2 and NLRP3. Western blot and multiplex immunofluorescence staining were used to demonstrate the molecular mechanism by which Sal alleviates hypoxic BBB injury via modulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. In vitro, a CoCl₂ induced hypoxic model was established in bEnd.3 cells. CCK-8 assay, EdU staining and LDH release assay were used to evaluate the effects of Sal on proliferative activity of hypoxic bEnd.3 cells. DCFH-DA and JC-1 staining were applied to detect intracellular ROS levels and mitochondrial membrane potential. Label-free cellular imaging enabled continuous monitoring of mitochondrial morphological changes under hypoxia, and TEM further observed mitochondrial ultrastructural damage. Mitochondrial superoxide, mPTP and mtDNA staining together with SOD, MDA, GSH-PX and ATP quantification were performed to analyze hypoxia and Sal mediated changes in mitochondrial function. Furthermore, cell scratch wound healing, tube-formation and cell migration assays examined hypoxic vascular functional changes, while TEER resistance and FITC-dextran permeability assays assessed paracellular permeability. Western blot combined with multiplex flow cytometry was used to analyze Sal regulated expression of Lcn2, NLRP3 and downstream inflammatory factors. In addition, the Lcn2 inhibitor ZINC00640089 and target specific siRNA were employed to validate the regulatory role of Lcn2 on NLRP3. Finally, CETSA was further performed to determine the binding stability of Sal to Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis proteins. The results demonstrated that Sal exerted robust anti-hypoxic neuroprotective effects in HHBI mice by alleviating cerebral hypoxic stress, suppressing neuroinflammation, improving cerebral microcirculation, maintaining BBB integrity, and upregulating TJ proteins. In vivo data indicated that Sal intervention markedly improved basal respiratory function and alleviated cerebral memory and cognitive impairment in HHBI mice. Meanwhile, Sal effectively mitigated cerebral inflammatory injury induced by acute hypoxic stimulation and restored excessive BBB hyperpermeability. Mechanistically, acute endothelial inflammation and TJ disruption serve as key drivers of HHBI progression, which is predominantly modulated by aberrant activation of the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. Combined molecular docking, DFT calculation, LSPR detection and alanine scanning analyses confirmed the high-affinity and stable binding of Sal to core proteins of the Lcn2-NLRP3 axis. Western blot and immunofluorescence staining further revealed that Sal effectively alleviated BBB damage by negatively regulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling cascade, and verified the favorable colocalization of Lcn2 with cerebral vascular endothelium. In vitro experiments showed that Sal markedly reversed hypoxia-triggered mitochondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by reduced mitochondrial superoxide accumulation, inhibited mPTP opening and mtDNA leakage, as well as restored MMP, ATP synthesis, and balanced levels of SOD, MDA and GSH-PX, thereby suppressing apoptosis in hypoxic bEnd.3 cells. Furthermore, Sal stabilized endothelial vascular structure and barrier function, increased transepithelial electrical resistance and elevated TJ protein expression in hypoxic endothelial cells. Multiplex flow cytometry further validated the regulatory effect of Sal on hypoxic inflammatory responses. Moreover, intervention with the Lcn2 inhibitor ZINC00640089 and Lcn2-specific siRNA further confirmed that Lcn2 acts as an indispensable upstream regulator of NLRP3 inflammasome activation and subsequent inflammatory cascades. Collectively, this study demonstrated that Sal ameliorates acute hypoxia‑induced mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby inhibiting excessive Lcn2 accumulation, suppressing subsequent NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and activation, and blocking downstream inflammatory cascade amplification. These effects ultimately alleviate vascular structural and functional damage, thereby exerting prominent preventive and therapeutic effects against HHBI.

title: Critical advances and translational bottlenecks of gut microbiota-gut-brain axis targeted therapy for neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders.
abstract: Neurological diseases have become a major global public health burden. Existing central nervous system-targeted therapies can only alleviate clinical symptoms but fail to halt the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, presenting mechanistic limitations and therapeutic bottlenecks. The gut microbiota participates in the regulation of central nervous system (CNS) homeostasis and neuropathological processes via the microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA). Notably, dysbiosis may induce damage to the blood-brain barrier, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and immune imbalance, thereby mediating the onset and progression of various neurological diseases, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease (AD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and multiple sclerosis (MS). This article provides a systematic review of the core mechanisms by which the gut microbiome regulates neurological diseases, including inflammation regulation, oxidative stress responses, and neuroendocrine remodeling mediated by microbial metabolites. It also comprehensively summarizes the research progress, application advantages, and existing limitations of novel gut-targeted interventions, such as probiotics, prebiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), dietary interventions, and live biological therapies. At the same time, the article critically examines key bottlenecks prevalent in the field: the causal relationship between the microbiota and disease remains unclear; there is a significant translational gap between animal and human studies; there is a lack of unified standards for multi-omics analysis systems; and interference from confounding factors such as age, diet, and medications is significant. Existing research indicates that gut microbiota interventions complement traditional symptomatic treatments and hold promising prospects for early disease intervention and adjunctive therapy for refractory patients. Future efforts should integrate multi-omics and artificial intelligence technologies to decipher the causal networks governing gut-central nervous system regulation, establish standardized research frameworks, advance the clinical translation of precision gut microbiota therapies, and provide new approaches for the comprehensive prevention, control, and personalized treatment of neurological disorders.

title: Restoration of BDNF/TrkB signaling rescues presynaptic dysfunction in GM1 gangliosidosis iPSC-derived neurons.
abstract: GM1 gangliosidosis is a lysosomal storage disease characterized by progressive neurodegeneration and severe central nervous system (CNS) dysfunction. Although the abnormal intracellular accumulation of GM1 ganglioside is recognized as a major pathological feature, the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal dysfunction remain unclear. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) plays essential roles in CNS development and the maintenance of synaptic function and plasticity; however, its contribution to the pathology of lysosomal storage diseases remains unclear. We previously identified a marked impairment of neurotransmitter release in GM1 gangliosidosis neurons, accompanied by reduced expression of synapse-related molecules. In this study, we investigated the potential involvement of endogenous BDNF signaling in synaptic dysfunction using human iPSC-derived neurons. We found that endogenous BDNF expression was significantly reduced in GM1 gangliosidosis neurons, accompanied by a marked decrease in full-length tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB), a key mediator of BDNF signaling. Further, the gene expression of synapse-related molecules involved in neurotransmitter release, including SNAP25 and VAMP2, was reduced. Importantly, exogenous BDNF supplementation ameliorated presynaptic dysfunction and substantially restored the expression of synapse-related molecules, which were reduced in disease neurons. Furthermore, 7,8-dihydroxyflavone (7,8-DHF), a selective TrkB agonist, markedly reversed presynaptic dysfunction. These findings suggest that impaired BDNF/TrkB signaling contributes to presynaptic dysfunction in GM1 gangliosidosis and identify the enhancement of this pathway as a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: Biobehavioral correlates of perceived health-related quality of life in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis: Toward an extended framework for understanding health impact.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an immune-mediated central nervous system disorder; relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) is the most common form. Self-perceived health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has been linked to psycho-behavioral and immunological factors, but their interplay remains unclear. We examined psycho-behavioral, clinical, and immunological correlates of perceived physical and mental health. In this cross-sectional study, 85 patients with RRMS (78% female; mean age 40.6 ± 10.3 years; predominantly mild disability) were assessed for fatigue, sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, anxiety/depression symptoms, and perceived cognitive dysfunction. Blood samples were analyzed for complete blood counts and, in a subgroup, lymphocyte subpopulations; the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) was calculated. HRQoL was measured using the SF-36 Physical and Mental Component Summaries (PCS and MCS). Hierarchical linear regression models included sociodemographic, clinical, and treatment-class covariates, with sensitivity analyses. Disability, fatigue, and depressive symptoms were associated with lower PCS, and sleep disturbances and depressive symptoms with lower MCS. Higher lymphocyte count was associated with higher MCS (β = +0.268, p = 0.006; ΔR2 = 0.030), consistently across all four sensitivity analyses. SII was not significantly associated with either outcome. In exploratory flow-cytometry analyses (n = 33-34), NK cells were associated with PCS (β = +0.345, p = 0.003), but not significantly with MCS. HRQoL in RRMS showed psychological and clinical associations, with an additional lymphocyte-MCS association. The clinical relevance of the immune findings, including the exploratory NK-PCS association, requires further investigation.

title: A sex-specific modification of the SARA questionnaire for obstructive sleep apnea screening: Comparative validation against six other tools in the HypnoLaus cohort.
abstract: and objectivesObstructive sleep apnea is significantly underdiagnosed in women, partly because existing screening tools were developed in male-predominant cohorts and may fail to capture female-specific clinical presentations. We used the HypnoLaus population-based cohort (n = 1540; 718 women, 822 men) to evaluate seven OSA screening tools in this cross-sectional study and assessed whether adding menopausal status to SARA enhances diagnostic accuracy. Moderate-to-severe OSA was defined as AHI ≥ 15 events per hour on polysomnography. The study included 1540 participants (718 women, 822 men). NoSAS and the updated SARA demonstrated the highest overall discriminative performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), 0.741 (95% CI, 0.718-0.764) and 0.693 (95% CI, 0.669-0.716), respectively, followed by original SARA (AUC, 0.684), Berlin (0.635), SONA (0.579), STOP-Bang (0.575), and ESS (0.507). Incorporation of menopausal status improved discrimination of SARA in women (AUC 0.675 vs. 0.627; p = 0.001). Although NoSAS showed the highest overall AUC, updated SARA performed more consistently across sex-, age-, and BMI-defined phenotypes. In women ≤55 years, updated SARA showed higher discrimination than NoSAS (AUC 0.616 vs. 0.509; p = 0.014), and in lean women (BMI <25 kg/m2), updated SARA detected cases that NoSAS missed (sensitivity 42.3% vs. 0%). Sex-related differences affect OSA screening. Incorporating menopausal status into SARA improved OSA detection in women. At the same time, anthropometry-weighted tools such as NoSAS performed poorly in younger, leaner women, underscoring the limitations of anthropometry-based screening in these phenotypes.

title: Imagery-based fear conditioning and extinction learning in individuals with psychotic liability: an EEG study.
abstract: Pavlovian fear conditioning using aversive imagery rather than physical stimuli as the unconditioned stimulus (US) provides a powerful paradigm to study fear learning in psychosis, in which threat expectations often develop in the absence of proximal external threats. This preregistered study aimed to identify behavioral, psychophysiological, and neural aberrancies in imagery-based fear acquisition and extinction learning associated with psychotic liability. Participants at-risk for psychosis (n = 70 with elevated psychosis proneness, n = 28 with verified clinical high-risk status) and non-clinical controls (n = 55) underwent an imagery-based fear conditioning paradigm. Participants learnt to produce aversive, neutral (US), or no imagery in response to cues (shapes) that were systematically paired with a different neutral face (conditioned stimulus; CS). Behavioral ratings, EEG (late positive potential; LPP), and psychophysiological responses (skin conductance responses; SCRs) were assessed. The at-risk group showed more pronounced acquisition learning in fear and arousal ratings and LPPs than controls. This pattern was driven by elevated affect ratings to the CS+ that had been paired with aversive imagery. In contrast, explicit expectancy ratings indicated less CS discrimination in at-risk individuals. The at-risk group also showed reduced extinction learning in expectancy but faster extinction learning in fear and arousal ratings than controls. Psychotic liability is associated with an increased susceptibility to acquire fear through negative mental imagery, even in the absence of actual threat. These findings provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of psychosis, suggesting that imagined threat beliefs could contribute to delusion formation.

title: Epigenetic age acceleration in the brain and blood of people with epilepsy and in a mouse model of focal cortical dysplasia: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
abstract: People with epilepsy have reduced life expectancy and more age-related comorbidities, suggesting a link to faster biological ageing. Direct molecular evidence has been scarce. We applied DNA-methylation-based epigenetic clocks to brain and blood samples from 324 unique individuals with structural or genetic epilepsy and 65 non-epilepsy controls, and to an in utero electroporation mouse model of somatic mTOR pathway activation (etiocopy of human FCD type 2) sampled before and after seizure onset. Epigenetic age acceleration was defined as the residual from a robust regression on chronological age, sex, cell-type composition, and array type. Relative telomere length was measured in the mouse model to independently validate biological ageing. In brain, epigenetic age acceleration was consistent across structural lesion types (median +7.3 years, p < 0.0001), most pronounced in GG (+10 years, adj. p < 0.0001), followed by MOGHE (+8.1 years, adj. p < 0.0001), TLE (+6.6 years, adj. p < 0.001), and FCD (+5.6 years, adj. p < 0.001). In blood, age acceleration was not significant after adjustment for cell composition, age, and sex (median +0.7 years, p = 0.20), except in FCD (+2.3 years, adj. p < 0.05). Across structural epilepsies, acceleration was greater in brain than in blood (median +7.3 vs. + 1.4 years, p < 0.0001). Available VPA-exposure data (n = 175) was not significantly associated with age acceleration. In a drug-naïve mTOR mouse model, mutant epileptic brains, but not blood, showed epigenetic age acceleration (adj. p < 0.05). Ageing signatures were already detectable in brains of animals in the pre-seizure latency phase and were independently supported by shortened relative telomere length (adj. p = 0.05), indicating that biological ageing can precede overt epilepsy. Accelerated epigenetic ageing is a consistent feature of the epileptic brain in drug-resistant structural epilepsies and a candidate pathway for disease modification. The contribution of systemic ageing remains unresolved, and generalisability to other aetiologies will need to be further tested.
